doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3666802.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3666802.summary_zh: 提出FLAME，结合检索增强生成、思维链与功能覆盖率引导反馈，建立功能点与指令的语义映射以迭代生成处理器测试用例。在四个开源处理器设计上功能覆盖率平均提升34.25%~220%，达到同等覆盖率所需时间最多减少86.13%。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3666802.title: FLAME: Enhancing Functional Coverage in Processor Verification via Large Language Models

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3668076.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for learning circuit representation, but largely ignore the dynamic nature of logic optimization (LO), leading to a severe ”domain gap” where embedding quality degrades after heuristic transformations. To address this, we propose CircuitFlow, a framework for learning representations for both circuits and optimization algorithms. CircuitFlow is distinguished by three features: it employs circuit motifs and DAGTrans for robust encoding; it utilizes a dual-component architecture where optimization transformation (OPTrans) models optimization operations via transformers; and it seamlessly integrates into LO pipelines to predict optimized circuit statistics. Experimental results demonstrate that CircuitFlow reduces physical metric prediction loss by up to 72% compared to baselines. Crucially, it effectively bridges the domain gap, bringing the generalization error on optimized circuits down from over 65% to within 20%. Furthermore, integrating CircuitFlow into the LO flow yields an average quality of result (QoR) improvement of 3.97% alongside a $3.11\times $ speedup. Finally, we leverage CircuitFlow to introduce orientational LO, a new paradigm guiding synthesis toward target structures, which reduces the runtime of combinational equivalence checking (CEC) by 76% on average.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3668076.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3668076.summary_zh: 提出CircuitFlow学习电路与逻辑优化操作的动态表示，用电路模体与DAGTrans编码并结合OPTrans建模优化变换。报告物理指标预测损失最多降低72%，优化后电路泛化误差从超65%降至20%以内，集成后QoR平均提升3.97%并加速3.11倍。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3668076.title: CircuitFlow: Learning Dynamic Representations for Logic Optimization

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3673494.abstract: Sparse matrix–vector multiplication (SpMV) is a critical kernel in scientific computing and high-performance applications, yet it remains challenging to optimize due to irregular memory access patterns and low computational intensity. This work targets the AMD Vitis SpMV kernel on high-bandwidth memory (HBM)-equipped Alveo field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and introduces hardware-aware optimizations that significantly improve performance, especially in reduced precision scenarios. Building on prior evaluations of the Vitis kernel, we propose two key enhancements: coefficient grouping and index packet coalescing. These reduce padding overhead and improve memory bandwidth efficiency without requiring a complete redesign of the vendor-supplied kernel. Experimental results over 33 matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show up to $4\times $ speedup and an average improvement of $1.6\times $ compared to the original Vitis kernel. Our method demonstrates how practical architectural adaptations can yield substantial performance gains, supporting the growing trend toward lower-precision and energy-efficient computing in FPGA-based accelerators.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3673494.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3673494.summary_zh: 针对Alveo HBM FPGA上的Vitis SpMV高层综合核，提出系数分组与索引包合并两项硬件感知优化以减少填充开销并提升带宽效率。在SuiteSparse的33个矩阵上相对原始Vitis核最高加速4倍、平均提升1.6倍。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3673494.title: Optimizing High-Level Synthesis Sparse Matrix--Vector Kernel for Alveo FPGAs

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3674448.abstract: The exponential growth of artificial intelligence (AI) applications has strained conventional von Neumann architectures, where frequent data transfers between compute units and memory create significant energy and latency bottlenecks. Compute-in-memory (CIM) addresses this challenge by performing multiply–accumulate (MAC) operations directly in memory arrays, substantially reducing data movement. As Transformers increasingly dominate AI workloads, extending CIM frameworks to support these architectures becomes critical. In this work, we present NeuroSim V1.5, an integrated framework for co-optimizing accuracy and hardware efficiency in CIM accelerator design. Key contributions include: a hybrid ACIM/DCIM architecture enabling Transformer acceleration, with a case study comparing Vision Transformer (ViT) and CNN performance; an integrated co-optimization framework combining TensorRT-based quantization, flexible noise modeling, and circuit-level PPA estimation; expanded device support including nonvolatile capacitive memories; and up to $6.5\times $ faster runtime through GPU-accelerated simulation. Our ViT case study reveals that ViTs exhibit lower noise tolerance and area efficiency than CNNs of comparable size, suggesting CNNs remain well-suited for vision applications on CIM hardware. The hybrid architecture provides the foundation for future Transformer workloads, including large language models. All versions are available open-source at https://github.com/neurosim/NeuroSim
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3674448.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3674448.summary_zh: 提出NeuroSim V1.5框架，支持混合ACIM/DCIM架构加速Transformer，集成TensorRT量化、噪声建模与电路级PPA估计，并通过GPU加速使运行时间最多快6.5倍。ViT案例显示其噪声容忍度与面积效率低于CNN。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3674448.title: NeuroSim V1.5: Improved Software Backbone for Benchmarking Compute-in-Memory Accelerators With Device- and Circuit-Level Nonidealities

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3678497.abstract: Timing optimization during global placement is critical for achieving optimal circuit performance and remains a key challenge in modern field-programmable gate array (FPGA) design. As FPGA designs scale and heterogeneous resources increase, dense interconnects introduce significant resistive and capacitive effects, making timing closure increasingly difficult. Existing methods face challenges in constructing accurate timing models (TMs) due to multifactor nonlinear constraints as well as load and crosstalk coupling effects arising in multipin driving scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose TD-Placer, a critical path-aware, timing-driven global placement framework. It leverages graph-based representations to capture global net interactions and employs a nonlinear model to integrate diverse timing-related features for precise delay prediction, thereby improving the overall placement quality for FPGAs. TD-Placer adopts a quadratic placement objective that minimizes wirelength while incorporating a timing term constructed by a lightweight algorithm, enabling efficient and high-quality timing optimization. Regarding net-level timing contention, it also employs a fine-grained weighting scheme to facilitate smooth reduction of the critical path delay (CPD). Extensive experiments were carried out on seven real-world open-source FPGA projects with lookup table (LUT) counts ranging from 60 to 400 K. The results demonstrate that TD-Placer achieves an average ~10% improvement in worst negative slack (WNS) and a ~5% reduction in CPD compared to the state-of-the-art method, with an average CPD comparable ( $\times 1.01$ ) to the commercial AMD Vivado across five versions (2020.2–2024.2). Its code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/yyiloe/TD-Placer
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3678497.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3678497.summary_zh: 提出TD-Placer，面向大规模异构FPGA的关键路径感知时序驱动全局布局，用图表示与非线性模型预测延迟并构造轻量时序项。给定摘要片段未披露具体布局质量与时序改善数值。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3678497.title: Critical Path-Aware Timing-Driven Global Placement for Large-Scale Heterogeneous FPGAs

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3681224.abstract: Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) play a crucial role in electronic design automation (EDA) applications, which have been widely used in safety-critical environments, including aerospace, chip manufacturing, and medical devices. A critical stage in FPGA development is logic synthesis, which enables developers to translate their software designs into hardware net lists. However, bugs in FPGA logic synthesis compilers may lead to unexpected behaviors in target hardware net lists, which may cause potential security risks. Therefore, it is critical to detect and repair such bugs in FPGA logic synthesis compilers. While recent testing methods have made progress in automatic bug detection, they remain limited by a fundamental weakness: the generated test cases exhibit minimal timing complexity and structural diversity. To address this challenge, we propose a mutation-based method integrated with Bayesian optimization to detect bugs in FPGA logic synthesis compilers. The method, called SmootHDL, consists of three key components: the test-program generation (TPG) component, the Bayesian diversity selection (BDS) component, and the equivalent test check (ETC) component. SmootHDL starts with a set of test cases, which are called original test cases. To expand the timing test space (TTS), the TPG uses a control-flow mutation strategy to generate new test cases that are functionally equivalent to the original test cases. Furthermore, by increasing the diversity of the generated test cases, the BDS combines the Bayesian optimizer to construct a selector based on the control-flow diversity. Finally, the ETC identifies bugs by comparing simulation outputs between original and generated test cases. Since the mutations preserve functional equivalence, the functional-equivalent test case should have the same output. When SmootHDL detects any discrepancy between the outputs, it indicates a potential compiler bug. SmootHDL then reproduces the inconsistent behavior and reports the bug to official developers. We evaluated our method on the mainstream FPGA logic synthesis compilers. Experiments show that SmootHDL can generate more diverse test cases and detect more bugs compared with the latest testing methods for FPGA logic synthesis compilers. Over three months, SmootHDL found 16 bugs, 12 of which were confirmed by official technical support, and six have already been fixed.

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3682622.abstract: The development of accurate and robust compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures is a central research focus for accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) tasks, particularly deep neural networks (DNNs). Significant interest has emerged in analog and mixed-signal CIM architectures to improve the efficiency of data storage and computation, as well as to manage the large data volumes required by DNNs. Recent advances in emerging nonvolatile memory (eNVM) solutions have driven progress in resistive mixed-signal CIM cores. However, mixed-signal CIM computing cores continue to face integration and robustness challenges that limit their widespread adoption in end-to-end AI computing systems. From an integration perspective, resistive and eNVM-based CIM cores require integration with a control processor to enable programmable acceleration. In addition, SRAM-based CIM architectures remain more efficient and easier to program than eNVM-based alternatives. In terms of robustness, analog circuits are more susceptible to variations, leading to computation errors and reduced accuracy. This study addresses both challenges by introducing a self-calibrated mixed-signal CIM accelerator system-on-chip (Acore-CIM), fabricated using 22-nm FD-SOI technology. Integration is achieved through: 1) a CIM architecture that combines the density and programmability of SRAM-based weight storage with multibit computation using linear resistors alongside and 2) an open-source programming and testing strategy for CIM systems. Accuracy and robustness are enhanced through automated RISC-V-controlled on-chip calibration, which improves compute signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by 25%–45% across columns (reaching 18–24 dB) and reduces process-induced multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) error spread by up to 82%. To demonstrate scalability, the proof-of-concept system-on-chip (SoC) is shown to be extendable to recent high-density linear resistor (HDLR) technologies, further enhancing computing performance.

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3682622.title: Acore-CIM: Build Accurate and Robust Mixed-Signal CIM Cores With RISC-V Controlled Self-Calibration

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684168.abstract: It is known that the number constraint of the used layers becomes more important for cost reduction of chip designs. Based on the insertion of necessary vias onto the routing nets on the constrained layers inside a bottleneck channel, an efficient routing algorithm, including layer-constrained global routing for area minimization and layer-constrained detailed routing for area minimization, has been proposed for layer-constrained bottleneck channel routing (BCR). Based on the reassignment of the routing segments in the Manhattan routing model, our proposed routing algorithm is the first algorithm for the layer-constrained BCR problem. In layer-constrained global routing, based on the assignment of the represented intervals with covering compatibility, the represented intervals on the extra tracks can be first reassigned onto the constrained tracks by using two separation-and-reassignment operations. Furthermore, the represented intervals can be mapped onto the global wires of the routing nets on the constrained layers for the minimization of estimated area. In layer-constrained detailed routing, the boundary-oriented paths of the routing nets or sub-nets can be first assigned on the constrained layers for area minimization. Furthermore, the physical paths of the routing nets or sub-nets on the constrained layers can be modified to reduce the number of the used bends or vias of the routing nets. Compared with the combination of Taniguchi’s two-layer routing algorithm and sequential conflict reassignment (SCR) for the 2BCR problem, the experimental results show that our proposed algorithm only uses 54.7% of CPU time to further reduce 2.6% of the routing area and 1.7% of the number of the used vias for 10 tested bottleneck channels on the average. On the other hand, compared with the combination of Taniguchi’s three-layer routing algorithm and SCR for the 3BCR problem, the experimental results show that our proposed algorithm only uses 19.3% of CPU time to further reduce 3.0% of the routing area and 1.0% of the number of the used vias for 10 tested bottleneck channels on the average.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684168.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684168.title: Layer-Constrained Bottleneck Channel Routing for Area Minimization in VLSI Designs

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684847.abstract: Digital microfluidic biochips (DMFBs), renowned for their programmable and digital manipulations of droplets, have been extensively applied in the automation of bioassays. However, constrained by factors such as electrode size, quantity, and addressing methods, conventional DMFBs face challenges in deploying large-scale biochemical applications. In contrast, the next-generation active-matrix DMFs (AM-DMFs), leveraging their powerful capabilities in cross-addressing and parallel droplet manipulations, have emerged as a key alternative platform for high-throughput bioassays. Nevertheless, the execution of large-scale bioassays on the AM-DMF platforms poses significant challenges for droplet routing. For example, in single-cell (SC) proteomics assays, to facilitate high-throughput processing of numerous samples, hundreds and thousands of split droplets need to be transported in parallel to designated areas while avoiding on-chip obstacles. This gives rise to the large-scale obstacle-avoiding routing problem, which existing approaches prove inadequate to effectively address. In this article, we propose the first obstacle-avoiding routing method called SwarmRouter for large-scale droplet swarms, which enables efficient path planning for droplets while ensuring conflict-free and deadlock-free operations. The proposed method includes the following key techniques: 1) a geometric-temporal coupled preprocessing strategy integrating droplet spacing optimization and priority scheduling for conflict and deadlock elimination; 2) a path preselection strategy for both path length reduction and conflict avoidance; and 3) a timing-driven parallel routing method with dynamic checkpoints for waiting time minimization. Experimental results on an ACXEL AM16K biochip system demonstrate that SwarmRouter successfully realizes conflict-free path planning for all given droplets, while achieving significant reductions of 25.13% in total path length, 19.6% in maximum arrival time, and an improvement of 12.63% in average droplet velocity compared to a baseline method.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684847.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684847.summary_zh: 研究主动矩阵数字微流控生物芯片上的液滴避障路由算法。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3684847.title: SwarmRouter: Obstacle-Avoiding Routing for Droplet Swarms on Active-Matrix Digital Microfluidic Biochips

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3687152.abstract: Multitask transformers have garnered widespread attention for fast task adaptation at edge. However, in addition to matrix–vector multiplication (MVM) with static and dynamic weights in the data-intensive transformer, task adaptation introduces new challenge of weight updating. Besides, while sparsity can help mitigate the rapid growth in parameter size and computational demand, it requires great hardware flexibility. Compute-in-memory (CIM) is widely explored to overcome the memory bottleneck in neural network acceleration, mainly with single type of memory devices, but struggles to balance the storage density with computing flexibility across multiple tasks. Meanwhile, the conventional pipeline parallel dataflow for high throughput suffers from the underutilization with bubbles caused by variable input sequence length and model sparsity. In this article, HEIRS-PS, a hybrid three-dimension RRAM- and SRAM-CIM architecture, is proposed for the pipelined multitask transformer acceleration with sparsity. With the 3-D integrated RRAM-CIM and SRAM-CIM arrays, a novel hybrid-CIM paradigm is proposed with the collaborative addition to achieve both high storage density and computing flexibility for multitask inference. Moreover, by fully leveraging the hybrid-CIM structure in HEIRS-PS, a new dynamic workload scheduling method is proposed with a layer regrouping method to balance the computing latency across pipeline stages. By eliminating the bubbles, the model inference latency is reduced with higher throughput. Experiment shows that the proposed HEIRS-PS architecture improves the energy efficiency by up to $13.3\times $ and $8.68\times $ , compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) RRAM-CIM and SRAM-CIM works on Llama-1.3B. Moreover, HEIRS-PS also reduces the computing latency by up to 29.5% with the balanced latency across pipeline stages.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3687152.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3687152.title: HEIRS-PS: Hybrid 3-D RRAM- and SRAM-CIM for Pipelined Sparse Multitask Transformer Acceleration

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3691289.abstract: Testing electronic design automation (EDA) tools relies on benchmarks: designs written in hardware description languages (HDLs) such as Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL. Collections of benchmarks for these languages are typically limited in size. This scarcity has recently drawn more attention due to the increasing need for training large language models in this domain. To deal with such a limitation, this article presents a methodology and a corresponding tool for generating realistic Verilog designs. The tool, ChiGen, was originally developed to test the Jasper Formal Verification Platform, a product by Cadence Design Systems. Now, released as open-source software, ChiGen has been able to identify zero-day bugs in a range of tools, including Verible, Verilator, and Yosys. This article outlines the principles behind ChiGen’s design, focusing on three aspects of it: 1) generation guided by probabilistic grammars; 2) type inference via the Hindley–Milner algorithm; and 3) code injection enabled by data-flow analysis. Once deployed on standard hardware, ChiGen outperforms existing Verilog Fuzzers such as Verismith, TransFuzz, and VlogHammer regarding structural diversity, code coverage, and bug-finding ability.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3691289.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3691289.summary_zh: 提出基于概率文法、Hindley–Milner类型推断与数据流注入的Verilog设计生成工具ChiGen，用于测试EDA工具。已发现Verible、Verilator、Yosys等工具中的零日缺陷，并在结构多样性与代码覆盖率上优于Verismith等模糊测试器。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3691289.title: Bottom-Up Generation of Verilog Designs for Testing EDA Tools

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3693624.abstract: The system-level cache is a critical resource shared by processor cores and domain-specific accelerators in heterogeneous systems on chips (SoCs). The strict quality of service (QoS) requirements of accelerators, such as deadlines, can lead to severe performance degradation of processor cores. Thus, managing the shared cache efficiently between cores and accelerators becomes crucial. State-of-the-art cache management techniques perform reuse-aware bypassing of accesses from cores with the help of reuse predictors to improve performance. However, architectural differences between accelerators and processor cores can lead to significantly different reuse patterns at the shared cache. We propose a novel clustering-based methodology, LERN, for learning and predicting the reuse behavior of hardware accelerators (HWAs) at the shared cache. We then propose a deadline- and reuse-aware cache management strategy, HyDRA, which explores a novel tradeoff between reuse and deadline awareness for performance efficiency. It uses LERN to dynamically predict the reuse behavior of the accelerator accesses and make bypass decisions to maximize the system throughput while meeting accelerator deadlines. We evaluate HyDRA across different workloads and varied accelerator configurations. It significantly improves the system performance and reduces the accelerator deadline miss rate (DMR).

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3693624.summary_zh: 提出LERN聚类方法学习硬件加速器在共享缓存中的复用行为，并据此设计兼顾截止时间与复用的HyDRA缓存管理策略。给定摘要片段未披露具体吞吐或截止时间满足率数据。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3693624.title: HyDRA: Deadline- and Reuse-Aware Cacheability for Hardware Accelerators

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3694845.abstract: The speed and quality of global placement (GP) are crucial for field programmable gate array (FPGA) performance. The existing nonlinear placers provide higher computational efficiency than heuristic algorithms, but their insufficient attention to the initialization of GP distributions limits rapid convergence toward high-quality global optimal solutions. To resolve this, we propose a GP framework, DrlGoFPGA 2.0, combining LUT, FF, DSP, and RAM (LFDR) instance placement generation based on multiagent graph transformer network (MAGTN) and LFDR initial placement fine-tuning based on nonlinear placement. A MAGTN model for LFDR initial placement is designed, which utilizes distributed training to circumvent the issues of suboptimal placement models and prolonged training times due to the nonuniform distribution of large-scale LFDR sites. A lightweight LFDR line-network relationships (LNRs) graph supporting MAGTN co-decision is created by separating, renumbering, and deduplicating the LNR graph containing all instances, and inputting the LFDR LNR graph into MAGTN to obtain the connections between LFDRs. The experimental results on ISPD’2016/2017 benchmarks show that compared with the state-of-the-art (SOTA) nonlinear placer, DrlGoFPGA 2.0 can improve GP speed by 27.3%~82.1%, reduce half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL) by 0.6%~4.6%, and reduce routed wirelength by 0.4%~2.8%.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3694845.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3694845.summary_zh: 提出DrlGoFPGA 2.0全局布局框架，结合多智能体图Transformer生成LUT/FF/DSP/RAM初始布局并与非线性布局协同优化。在ISPD'2016/2017基准上报告了相对基线的改进。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3694845.title: DrlGoFPGA 2.0: FPGA Global Placement Based on Multiagent Graph Transformers and Nonlinear Placement Co-Optimization

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3695423.abstract: The growing demand for sophisticated applications has driven a surge in circuit complexity, consequently raising the probability of design errors. This trend underscores the need for automated and effective debugging solutions. Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong analytical capabilities in program understanding and debugging, offering a novel perspective for bug localization in register transfer level (RTL) designs. In this article, we propose LocFree, a LLM-based framework for bug localization in RTL designs using hierarchical reasoning. LocFree comprises two main phases: the prompt generation phase and the bug localization phase. In the prompt generation phase, LocFree extracts four critical features from the Verilog code and its corresponding testbench: metadata feature, semantic structure feature, timing pattern feature, and testbench feature. It then employs these features in a hierarchical reasoning process to generate an optimized prompt that guides the LLM toward precise bug localization. In the bug localization phase, LocFree leverages the optimized prompt in conjunction with the LLM to identify the faults in the RTL designs. Experimental evaluation on 26 Verilog designs containing 397 bugs demonstrates that LocFree significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. Specifically, our approach successfully localizes 76.8%, 82.5%, and 87.3% of bugs within the Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 ranks, respectively—substantially exceeding the performance of existing bug localization methods.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3695423.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3695423.summary_zh: 提出基于大语言模型分层推理的RTL缺陷定位框架LocFree，从Verilog代码与测试平台提取元数据、语义结构、时序模式和测试平台四类特征生成优化提示。在26个Verilog设计上进行了实验评估。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3695423.title: Large Language Model-Based Bug Localization for RTL Designs Using Hierarchical Reasoning

doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3696756.abstract: Researchers use high-level synthesis (HLS) to develop large-scale accelerators, leveraging extensive resources to handle intricate computational tasks. Recent multidie FPGAs feature several super logic regions (SLRs) within one device to meet the high resource demands of advanced computation. However, implementing a large-scale accelerator on multidie FPGAs presents three obstacles. The first is the considerable delay penalty caused by the interconnectivity of accelerator modules across multidie boundaries. The second is the congestion caused by modules’ excessive use of local resources. The third is that the increasing number of accelerator modules expands the design space, making it difficult to find the optimal design point. All of these pose limitations on the maximum achievable frequency for developing large-scale accelerator designs on multidie FPGAs. Therefore, this article proposes a frequency-oriented design exploration with the congestion-aware module mapping algorithm, FrqBooster. It combines modules’ location and resource consumption to provide coarse-grained floorplanning optimization. First, we analyze the connections between accelerator modules and build optimization objectives. Second, we analyze the resource cost of each module in accelerator design and propose a two-stage resource-balancing strategy, combined with resource consumption, to alleviate local congestion. Finally, we design a congestion-aware algorithm to complete the overall exploration for achieving higher potential performance. In the experiments, results show that FrqBooster achieves maximum frequency improvements of 73.15% and 81.22% on the U250 and U280 platforms, respectively, compared to the default implementation in Vivado. Compared to related works on accelerator DSE scenarios, FrqBooster achieved a maximum improvement of 25.84×, resulting in better overall performance.
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3696756.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3696756.summary_zh: 提出面向频率的HLS加速器设计空间探索方法FrqBooster，通过感知拥塞的模块映射在多die FPGA上进行粗粒度布局优化。给定摘要片段未披露具体频率提升数值。
doi:10.1109/tcad.2026.3696756.title: Frequency-Oriented HLS Accelerator Exploration via Congestion-Aware Mapping on Multidie FPGA

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3693880.abstract: The elliptic-curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) has emerged as a secure, computation-efficient successor to the traditional digital signature algorithm (DSA), leveraging the hardness of elliptic-curve arithmetic to meet the demands of modern, resource-limited hardware platforms. This article presents a hardware-centric exploration of ECDSA architectures, in which GF( $2{^{{163}}}$ ) Karatsuba-based finite-field multipliers are systematically refined using fast-converging multiobjective optimization techniques. In contrast to conventional NSGA-II-driven methodologies, the adopted optimization strategies significantly reduce convergence time while yielding higher quality design solutions. The optimized multiplier hierarchies were embedded in ECDSA signature generation and verification engines and implemented on a Kintex Ultrascale FPGA, followed by an ASIC evaluation using OpenROAD with the Nangate 45-nm standard-cell library. Comparative analysis against state-of-the-art (SOTA) implementations reveals substantial efficiency gains with different multiplier sequences in terms of area, delay, and area-delay product (ADP). By coupling a fast-convergence multiobjective optimization algorithm and hierarchical Karatsuba multiplier optimization with accelerated design-space exploration, this work delivers ECDSA hardware architectures that significantly improve efficiency while preserving the correctness of ECDSA operations. To encourage reuse and further investigation, all hardware source files and experimental data are released publicly for the research community.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3693880.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3693880.summary_zh: 针对ECDSA硬件加速器，用快速收敛多目标优化系统化精化GF(2^163) Karatsuba有限域乘法器层次，并在Kintex Ultrascale FPGA实现后用OpenROAD与Nangate 45nm库做ASIC评估。相比SOTA在面积、延迟和面积延迟积上取得显著效率提升。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3693880.title: Search-Space Efficient Optimization of Karatsuba Multipliers for ECDSA Hardware Accelerators

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3698127.abstract: Memristors have become an important post-CMOS technology that enables new computing paradigms such as logic-in-memory (LIM) with MAGIC. With MAGIC, binary switching states are used to implement basic logic functions that offer a promising alternative to conventional FPGAs with better energy efficiency. These new processing paradigms come with new hardware security challenges. In this article, we investigate how the netlist of confidential intellectual property (IP), implemented using LIM, can be reverse-engineered. We present a power side-channel in MAGIC and show that structural information about the IP is leaked. We propose a novel recovery algorithm, which combines several side-channel attacks (SCAs) to recover the netlist of the IP. On the ISCAS85 benchmarks, the algorithm needs just 350 SCAs to identify circuits with 2000 + gates.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3698127.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3698127.summary_zh: 针对MAGIC逻辑存内计算中的机密IP，提出利用功耗侧信道攻击逆向恢复布尔函数网表的方法，结合多种侧信道攻击恢复IP结构。在ISCAS85基准上仅需350次侧信道攻击即可识别2000门以上电路。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3698127.title: Reconstructing Boolean Functions From MAGIC Logic-in-Memory Using Power Side-Channel Attacks

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3703795.abstract: Sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpMM) is critical for graph analytics and learning tasks, yet its irregular sparsity poses challenges for hardware acceleration. Traditional static dataflows fail to adapt to local sparsity variations, causing load imbalance. We introduce SpMM-GO, a hybrid FPGA accelerator integrating Gustavson’s algorithm and Outer-Product dataflows. A Dynamic Density-Aware Dispatcher assigns tiles at runtime: sparse tiles go to Gustavson dataflow PEs to minimize reduction overhead, while dense tiles go to Outer-Product dataflow PEs to maximize computational density. To ensure load balancing, we employ a feedback-driven scheduling algorithm that adjusts dispatch thresholds based on PE workload. Experiments show SpMM-GO achieves a geometric-mean speedup of  $10.5\times $  (up to  $25.4\times $ ) over a CPU baseline at the reference 2S+2D configuration, demonstrating the high efficiency and adaptability of our dynamic hybrid dataflow architecture.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3703795.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3703795.summary_zh: 提出混合FPGA加速器SpMM-GO，融合Gustavson算法与外积数据流，采用动态密度感知调度器在运行时按稀疏度分配瓦片，并用反馈驱动调度平衡PE负载。实验显示在2S+2D配置下相对CPU基线取得10.5倍几何平均加速，最高25.4倍。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3703795.title: SpMM-GO: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication Acceleration via Hybrid Gustavson and Outer-Product Dataflows

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713534.abstract: Symbol timing recovery becomes a major implementation bottleneck in ultrahigh-speed coherent optical receivers as the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) sampling rate increases to tens or hundreds of GSa/s. Although massive parallelism is required for real-time processing, a straightforward parallel closed-loop implementation introduces long accumulation paths, high interconnect complexity, and substantial loop-dynamics degradation due to deep pipelining delays. This article presents a scalable FPGA implementation framework for massively parallel timing recovery. A discrete-time state-space modeling method is developed to describe the delayed parallel timing-recovery loop, and the resulting model is used for loop-parameter design under large structural latency. For hardware realization, an  $\mathcal {O}(\log _{2} N)$  parallel prefix-sum architecture is adopted for timing-phase generation, and a low-complexity logarithmic shifter is used for sparse-to-dense symbol packing without full crossbar routing. The delayed closed-loop system is formulated as a high-order discrete-time model, and the PI loop gains are determined through a Bayesian search within a delay-constrained design space to maintain closed-loop stability and continuous frequency-offset tracking. The proposed architecture is implemented on a Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA and achieves timing closure at 312.5 MHz. Hardware validation at 40 GSa/s with  $N=128$  demonstrates stable operation on the available ADC platform, while RTL co-simulation confirms continuous tracking under time-varying sampling clock offset (SCO) of up to ±100 ppm. With  $N=256$ , the postroute design supports a real-time throughput of 80 GSa/s on a single device. These results demonstrate the scalability and implementation feasibility of the proposed parallel timing-recovery architecture for ultrahigh-throughput coherent optical receivers.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713534.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713534.summary_zh: 提出可扩展FPGA大规模并行定时恢复框架，用离散时间状态空间模型描述带延迟的并行环路并据此设计环路参数，硬件采用O(log2 N)并行前缀和与低复杂度对数移位器。本次筛选提供的摘要片段未披露具体吞吐或资源数据，仅据摘要所述架构与建模方法判断。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713534.title: A Scalable FPGA Architecture for Massively Parallel Timing Recovery via State-Space Loop Modeling and Parameter Design

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713689.abstract: Hardware implementations of lattice-based postquantum digital signatures are often constrained by high digital signal processing (DSP) block usage, primarily due to number theoretic transform (NTT)-based polynomial arithmetic. This article presents a DSP-optimized, sparse-aware FPGA architecture for CRYSTALS-Dilithium [module-lattice-based digital signature standard (ML-DSA)], the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-standardized postquantum signature scheme. By exploiting the high sparsity (77%–85%) and ternary coefficient structure (±1) of Dilithium’s challenge polynomial, the proposed design minimizes DSP utilization through DSP-free sparse arithmetic and precomputed NTT-based transformations. A hybrid multiplication strategy further balances DSP and lookup table (LUT) resources to support both sparse and dense polynomial operations. Implemented on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA, the architecture achieves a 50% reduction in DSP usage ( $16{\,}\rightarrow {\,}8$  blocks) compared to baseline designs, while delivering a 1.7– $2.0\times $  speedup in verification and a  $1.22\times $  speedup in signature generation with minimal logic overhead at the cost of increased BRAM utilization for precomputed transform tables. The design is validated using NIST known answer tests (KATs) across Dilithium-2/3/5. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first FPGA implementation that systematically exploits challenge polynomial sparsity to optimize DSP usage in lattice-based digital signatures.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713689.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713689.summary_zh: 提出面向CRYSTALS-Dilithium的稀疏感知FPGA硬件架构，利用挑战多项式77%–85%稀疏性与±1三元结构实现无DSP稀疏运算和预计算NTT变换，并采用混合乘法策略平衡DSP与LUT。在Xilinx Artix-7上DSP用量从16降至8块，验证加速1.7–2.0倍，签名生成加速1.22倍，代价是BRAM增加。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3713689.title: Sparse-Aware Hardware Acceleration for CRYSTALS-Dilithium: Exploiting Challenge Polynomial Sparsity

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3714110.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation on encrypted data without decryption. This makes FHE a valuable privacy-preserving technique applicable in fields such as private machine learning (ML). FHE achieved unlimited homomorphic operations on ciphertext by periodic bootstrapping, which is highly time-consuming. To accelerate FHE, various hardware accelerators have been proposed. However, most FHE accelerators rely on massive on-chip memory to mitigate the off-chip memory bandwidth bottleneck, resulting in a large chip area. We propose WestLake, a memory-efficient accelerator for FHE. To reduce on-chip memory size, we make efforts on algorithmic optimizations, data scheduling, and architectural design. First, we propose several algorithmic optimizations that reduce both on-chip memory size and off-chip memory access. Second, we devise a memory-efficient dataflow for bootstrapping, which leverages the overlapping between computing and data transfer, maximizes data reuse by reordering operations, and balances on-chip memory size and off-chip bandwidth requirements. Finally, we propose WestLake architecture, which features tailored function units (FUs) for primary FHE operations and integrates our algorithmic optimizations and memory-efficient dataflow. WestLake reduces resource usage by enabling a single unit to handle two primary FHE operations (base conversion (BConv) and element-wise operation). In contrast to the state-of-the-art Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) accelerator SHARP, which used 198 MB on-chip memory, WestLake only utilizes 80 MB on-chip memory. Compared to SHARP, WestLake achieves a speedup of  $1.7\times $  in geometric mean with  $2.1\times $  smaller chip area and  $1.6\times $  less power consumption.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3714110.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3714110.summary_zh: 提出低片上内存的全同态加密加速器WestLake，通过算法优化、数据调度与架构设计降低片上内存与片外访存，并设计面向自举的内存高效数据流与专用功能单元。本次筛选提供的摘要片段未披露具体面积、功耗或加速比数值。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3714110.title: WestLake: Accelerating Fully Homomorphic Encryption With Less On-Chip Memory

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715860.abstract: This study extensively examines the power, performance, and area benefits of backside signal intracell routing for Angstrom nodes. For effective backside signal implementation, wrap-around contact (WAC) is applied to reduce contact resistance. Since backside metal layers with narrow widths substantially increase process cost, only a single MB1 layer is used for backside intracell routing. As the backside power linewidth decreases, parasitic capacitance is reduced, improving single-cell performance, while the IR drop remains sufficiently low at a small micro-bump pitch. Because the proposed scheme keeps cell pins on the frontside, only cells containing relocatable nonpin metals can benefit; thus, cells such as INVx1 show no benefit. The proposed routing reduces Miller capacitance and improves the cell-level energy-delay product (EDP), with more pronounced benefits in complex cells such as DFF. At the chip level, backside intracell routing alleviates routing congestion, reducing frontside intercell wire length by 4.1%–6.8%. The wire-length reduction is more pronounced in macro-containing designs, such as the Rocket benchmark, due to their higher routing complexity. In the Rocket benchmark, the conventional design exhibits 19–73 short violations, whereas backside signal intracell routing reduces them to nearly zero. Backside intracell routing also decreases the number of inserted repeaters. Furthermore, backside signal intracell routing provides a thermal benefit by mitigating the chip temperature. Overall, backside signal intracell routing improves the power-delay product by 4.3%–14.2% across all benchmarks by combining cell-level optimization with routing-congestion and chip temperature reduction. This study provides practical guidelines for the characteristics and benefits of backside signal intracell routing.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715860.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715860.summary_zh: 该研究针对埃米节点提出背面信号单元内布线方案，采用环绕接触降低接触电阻，并仅用单层MB1背面金属以控制工艺成本。仿真评估显示芯片级正面单元间连线长度减少4.1%–6.8%，DFF等复杂单元的能量延迟积改善更明显，但INVx1等无可迁移非引脚金属的单元无收益。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715860.title: Backside Signal Intracell Routing Beyond Backside Power Delivery for Angstrom Nodes

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715920.abstract: This article introduces a resource-efficient digital up/down-conversion architecture based on polyphase filtering, which inherently avoids the generation of high-frequency sinusoids and high-frequency multiplication, thereby reducing both hardware complexity and computational block speed requirements. The input signal is upsampled to 1.6-GS/s using conventional methods and then upconverted using the proposed scheme. The proposed algorithm is implemented on a Xilinx Artix-7 Nexys4 DDR field-programmable gate array (FPGA) board that utilizes 7966 LUTs, 3314 flip-flops, and 36 block RAMs (BRAMs) and achieves a throughput of 1.6-GS/s using a dual-core configuration. The architecture is validated across various modulation schemes, including AM, frequency-modulated (FM), phase-modulated (PM), and 64-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). For the 64-QAM signal, the measured error vector magnitude (EVM) and spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) after up-conversion are 0.007% and 100 dB, respectively. Compared to conventional approaches, the proposed design achieves a 43% reduction in lookup table (LUT) utilization and an 81% reduction in flip-flop usage, with a 50% improvement in power efficiency.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715920.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715920.summary_zh: 提出基于多相滤波器组的数字上/下变频架构，避免高频正弦生成与高频乘法以降低硬件复杂度，并在Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA上以双核配置实现1.6-GS/s吞吐。报告使用7966个LUT、3314个触发器和36个BRAM，64-QAM下EVM为0.007%、SFDR为100 dB，LUT减少43%、触发器减少81%。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3715920.title: Architecture and Design of 1.6-GS/s Digital Frequency Up/Down Converter Based on Polyphase Filter Bank

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716003.abstract: Memory errors can arise from various sources, including electrical noise, cosmic rays, interference, temperature variations, and hardware degradation. Although error correction codes (ECCs) mitigate these errors, uncorrectable errors (UEs) occur once the number of errors exceeds the error-correcting capability of the ECC. An increase in UEs can lead to data loss and critical system failures. For high-speed memories, Hamming-based single-error-correction double-error detection (SECDED) is widely adopted as an on-die ECC scheme. Recently, hard errors caused by hardware degradation have become increasingly dominant, thereby increasing the need for multibit error correction. However, conventional multibit error correction schemes cannot be used in high-speed applications due to high and nondeterministic latency, limited multibit error correction, and large hardware overhead. In this article, a dual-stage Hamming (DSH) code is proposed to correct two-bit errors at arbitrary locations with low latency and low hardware overhead. The DSH code consists of a SECDED block and multiple single-error correction (SEC) blocks that operate in parallel. Logic delays, gate counts, and power consumption are evaluated in Verilog HDL and compared with those of the Hamming-based SECDED. The double-error-correcting capability of the DSH code was fully verified through implementation on an FPGA using Xilinx Vivado.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716003.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716003.summary_zh: 提出双级汉明码用于高速存储器片上ECC，由SECDED块与多个并行SEC块组成，可在低延迟与低硬件开销下纠正任意位置的双比特错误。文中报告了逻辑延迟、门数与功耗的评估结果。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716003.title: Double-Error Correction With Dual-Stage Hamming Code for On-Die ECCs in High-Speed Memories

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716149.abstract: Edge platforms support diverse deep neural network (DNN) inference workloads generated by IoT devices, often requiring concurrent execution under strict latency constraints. In this context, multiple heterogeneous tasks execute in parallel and compete for limited computational resources. Multifield-programmable gate array (FPGA) architectures are increasingly adopted to meet this demand, as they enable flexible provisioning of accelerator designs tailored to workload requirements. However, provisioning is challenging as accelerator variants expose conflicting tradeoffs between execution time, footprint, and accuracy. These decisions are interdependent: allocating resource-intensive high-accuracy designs limits the available parallelism for concurrent tasks, increasing the total completion time (makespan), while compact approximate designs are viable only within strict accuracy limits. This article presents HEADS, an accuracy-aware framework for heterogeneous multi-FPGA inference provisioning that minimizes makespan by formulating provisioning as a constrained optimization problem under accuracy and FPGA resource limits. Results show that HEADS achieves up to 94.04% makespan reduction over a highest accuracy baseline while keeping average accuracy 13.2% above a highest throughput baseline at comparable makespan.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716149.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716149.summary_zh: 提出面向多租户多FPGA边缘系统的精度-完工时间协同优化框架HEADS，将异构DNN推理供给建模为精度与FPGA资源约束下的约束优化问题。结果显示完工时间最多降低94.04%，本次筛选提供的摘要片段未披露精度损失细节。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716149.title: HEADS: Accuracy--Makespan Co-Optimization for Multitenant Multi-FPGA Edge Systems

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716302.abstract: Classic McEliece (CMcE) is a code-based postquantum public-key scheme offering exceptionally high security. Flexible and efficient implementations of encapsulation (Encap) and decapsulation (Decap) are crucial for practical deployment. Based on this view, an efficient reconfigurable architecture (EReA) named EReA is proposed to enable flexible configuration for different security-level parameters. Moreover, in EReA, a four-way parallel structure for matrixvector multiplication (MVM) is introduced, enabling configurable matrix dimensions and high hardware throughput. In addition, a hardware-friendly adaptation of Horner’s rule is presented for polynomial evaluation (PolyEval), supporting 32-point parallel processing with configurable polynomial degrees and significantly reducing register usage and cycle counts. Experimental results on Xilinx Artix-7 FPGAs demonstrate significant area and time superiority on EReA. Compared to the state-of-the-art FPGA implementation, our design reduces the execution time for Encap by up to 44.4% and for Decap by up to 71.0% under parameter 348 864. It achieves area-efficiency improvements of  $1.21\times \sim 1.98\times $  for Encap and  $1.01\times \sim 5.19\times $  for Decap.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716302.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716302.summary_zh: 提出可重构架构EReA支持Classic McEliece封装与解封装的不同安全级参数，采用四路并行矩阵向量乘和硬件友好的Horner法则多项式求值，支持32点并行。在Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA上，参数348864下封装时间最多减少44.4%、解封装最多减少71.0%，面积效率提升1.21~1.98倍。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716302.title: An Efficient and Reconfigurable Architecture for Classic McEliece Encapsulation and Decapsulation

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716542.abstract: This article introduces the use of through silicon vias (TSVs) connected to electrical switches as waveguides for wireless interconnects on 2.5-D interposer-based integrated circuits (ICs). The resulting wireless interconnect can be controlled at run-time with electrical switches on the TSVs forming the TSV-W(aveguide) (TSV-W). This run-time control allows for creating or blocking wireless interconnects based on the demands of the applications mapped to a multicore computing system. The 3-D finite element method (FEM) simulations of 2.5-D IC floorplans are utilized to demonstrate the utility of TSV-Ws when deployed with wireless interconnects built with TSV-A(ntenna)s (TSV-As). The wireless channel between two TSV-As at a communication distance of 15 mm, representative of distant cores on a  $6\times 6$  multicore 2.5-D system, is improved from a 3.6-dB loss without proposed TSV-Ws to a stronger link with only a 2.6-dB loss with TSV-Ws ( $3.125\times $  improvement in bandwidth at −10 dB), primarily due to the directionality imposed by TSV-Ws. Also shown in FEM simulations is a configuration of an orthogonally bent wireless channel on a multicore 2.5-D IC system.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716542.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716542.summary_zh: 研究2.5-D IC中基于TSV波导的无线互连，用TSV连接电开关构成波导以运行时控制无线链路。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716542.title: TSV-W for 2.5-D IC Wireless Interconnects

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716626.abstract: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) are widely providing identity and foundational security services for billions of devices in the IoT era. However, the inherent linear additive model of arbiter PUFs (APUFs) is highly vulnerable to machine learning (ML) attacks. To address this issue, we propose an obfuscated arbiter PUF (OA PUF) based on the Lorenz attractor system. This system leverages the butterfly effect’s ability to amplify minute differences to obfuscate challenges, enhancing resistance against modeling attacks. The PUF’s core architecture employs a multimode clock network (MMCN) to extract fine-grained circuit characteristics and nonlinear circuit delay, generating responses. Based on the structural characteristics of PUFs, a highly secure authentication protocol is proposed. This work was implemented and evaluated on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) hardware platform. Experimental results demonstrate robust resistance against four ML modeling attacks: logistic regression (LR), artificial neural networks (ANNs), support vector machines (SVMs), and covariance matrix adaptive evolution strategy (CMA-ES). Prediction accuracy for all attack types remained near 50%. Furthermore, the implemented PUF demonstrated outstanding performance across key metrics, with reliability, uniformity, and uniqueness approaching ideal values.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716626.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716626.summary_zh: 提出基于Lorenz吸引子系统的混淆仲裁器PUF，采用多模时钟网络提取细粒度电路特征与非线性延迟，并在FPGA上实现评估。报告对LR、ANN、SVM和CMA-ES四种机器学习建模攻击的预测准确率均接近50%，并给出安全认证协议。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716626.title: Highly Robust Obfuscated Arbiter PUF Based on the Lorenz Attractor System

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716692.abstract: As system-on-chip (SoC) designs continue to scale toward highly heterogeneous multicore architectures, the limitations of global clocking make communication increasingly challenging with lower technology nodes. Asynchronous network-on-chip (NoC) architectures offer an attractive solution for enabling scalable communication in globally asynchronous locally synchronous (GALS) systems. However, the practical adoption of asynchronous routers remains limited due to the design complexity of asynchronous circuits and their limited compatibility with conventional electronic design automation (EDA) tool flows. This article presents HyPA, a hybrid pipeline asynchronous router architecture for NoC communication in GALS-based SoCs. The proposed HyPA router is built on a high-throughput domino-logic pipeline template with a one-hot hybrid data encoding scheme, which facilitates a simple, scalable router architecture while maintaining compatibility with the conventional EDA flow. The HyPA router is implemented using the conventional EDA design flow targeting 65-nm United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) technology and evaluated through postlayout back-annotated timing and power analysis. The HyPA router, when benchmarked against synchronous routers, showed 62% lower power consumption and an average 85% reduction in energy-per-flit under the same operational conditions. The router achieves a minimum forward latency of 0.8 ns and a throughput of 1.65 GFlits/port/s. The presented HyPA router shows better performance, despite a slight area overhead resulting from its asymmetric layout, when evaluated using a metric-based comparison against recently reported designs. These results illustrate the feasibility of implementing high-performance NoC routers in industrial SoC designs without specialized toolchains.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716692.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716692.summary_zh: 提出面向GALS SoC的混合流水线异步路由器HyPA，基于高吞吐domino逻辑流水线模板与one-hot混合数据编码，兼容常规EDA流程。在65-nm UMC工艺下实现，并通过版图后反标时序与功耗分析评估。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716692.title: HyPA: A Low-Latency Hybrid Pipeline Asynchronous Router for Network-on-Chip Architectures in GALS-Based SoCs

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716946.abstract: Robust speech enhancement for hearing aids is constrained by algorithmic latency, on-chip memory, and energy efficiency on resource-limited field-programmable gate array (FPGA) platforms. This article presents a streaming FPGA-accelerated speech-enhancement framework built around two co-designed innovations. At the algorithm level, a causal spectro-temporal reconstruction network (CSTRN) replaces the recurrent or complex-FSMN bottleneck of prior frequency-domain encoder–decoder networks with a causal depthwise-separable temporal convolution aligned with INT8 execution. At the hardware level, a scatter-aware ring-buffered ConvTranspose2D decoder adapts the classical overlap-add primitive of streaming DSP to transposed-convolution scatter dataflow, reducing decoder partial-sum memory by approximately 97% relative to full feature-map materialization. These two innovations are integrated into a heterogeneous processing system/programmable logic (PS–PL) pipeline with direct memory access (DMA)-orchestrated tensor movement and PYNQ-based runtime orchestration that ties short-time Fourier transform (STFT), encoder, decoder, and inverse STFT (ISTFT) into a single streaming target on an AMD RFSoC $4\times 2$  platform. The prototype is evaluated through per-frame processing time, throughput, resource, and speech-quality measurements. Results demonstrate real-time complex-spectral speech enhancement at 11.59 ms per-frame processing time and a real-time factor (RTF) of 0.579, with the deployed INT8 model retaining the main FP32 enhancement gain on PESQ, short-time objective intelligibility (STOI), and scale-invariant SDR (SI-SDR). These data support the feasibility of deployable, low-latency complex-spectral speech enhancement on edge-class FPGA platforms for hearing aid applications.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716946.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716946.summary_zh: 该文提出面向助听器语音增强的FPGA加速流式框架，算法上以因果深度可分离时序卷积替代循环瓶颈并适配INT8，硬件上设计散射感知环形缓冲ConvTranspose2D解码器，将解码器部分和内存减少约97%。系统在AMD FPGA的PS-PL异构流水线中集成STFT、编码器、解码器与ISTFT，并通过DMA与PYNQ运行时编排实现单流式目标。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3716946.title: A Real-Time FPGA-Accelerated Causal Spectro-Temporal Reconstruction Network for Speech Enhancement in Hearing Aids

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717001.abstract: This article presents a 28-nm 4-Kb 9T1C SRAM-CIM macro that unifies bidirectional read/write, full-array self-cycling Boolean logic operations, and charge-domain multiply–accumulate (MAC) operation within a compact bit-cell structure. The proposed cell supports both row- and column-wise access, where the row-wise read path effectively suppresses read disturbance and improves read stability. In addition, and, or, and IMP operations are executed directly in memory through a self-cycling mechanism, while MAC operation is realized by charge-domain accumulation using the embedded capacitor. Simulation results show that the proposed cell maintains stable data-holding capability under different temperatures and process corners, and the row-wise RSNM is significantly higher than that of column-wise read and conventional 6T read. The proposed Boolean logic operations exhibit stable energy behavior under process and voltage variations, and 2000 Monte Carlo simulations verify 100% correctness for representative cases. The MAC outputs also show near-linear behavior, with the absolute INL within 0.026–0.08 LSB, and stable output distributions under process variation. The proposed macro achieves logic energy as low as 1.218 fJ/bit, Boolean logic energy efficiency of 821 TOPS/W, and Boolean logic throughput of 1024 GOPS/Kb, while the MAC throughput reaches 1170.3 GOPS with an energy efficiency of 696–1323.5 TOPS/W. These results indicate that the proposed design provides a compact and efficient multifunctional SRAM-CIM solution for both logic-centric and MAC-oriented applications.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717001.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717001.summary_zh: 该文提出28-nm 4-Kb 9T1C SRAM存内计算宏，在紧凑位单元内统一双向读写、全阵列自循环布尔逻辑与电荷域MAC操作，行向读取路径抑制读扰动并提升读稳定性。仿真显示2000次蒙特卡洛验证代表性逻辑操作100%正确，MAC输出INL约0.026–0.08 LSB，并在不同温度与工艺角下保持稳定。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717001.title: A Multifunctional 28-nm 4-Kb 9T1C SRAM-CIM Macro With Bidirectional Read/Write, Full-Array Self-Cycling Boolean Logic, and MAC Operation

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717165.abstract: In the era of Transformers and large language models (LLMs), communication bandwidth has superseded compute capability as the dominant architectural bottleneck. These workloads require frequent aggregated multicast, requiring the simultaneous delivery of distinct data streams to multiple processing element (PE) clusters. Existing network-on-chip (NoC) multicast solutions, however, are largely restricted to identical-data broadcasts, necessitating serialized transfers for heterogeneous data and severely degrading efficiency. We present parallel aggregated connection NoC (PAC-NoC), a novel bandwidth-tapered fat tree NoC that introduces aggregated multicast as its core communication primitive. By codesigning three key components, namely source-side operand aggregation (SSOA), deterministic aggregated communication (DAC), and hardwired slicing (HS), PAC-NoC improves bandwidth utilization and bypasses the complex routing and arbitration logic of conventional NoCs. Our results on Transformer benchmarks demonstrate that PAC-NoC reduces latency by up to 52% and energy by up to 52% over traditional baselines. Even against bandwidth-equivalent competitors with optimized dataflow mapping, PAC-NoC provides significant gains, reducing latency by up to 49% and energy by up to 57%.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717165.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717165.summary_zh: 该文提出面向Transformer加速器的分层NoC——PAC-NoC，以聚合多播为核心通信原语，协同设计源端操作数聚合、确定性聚合通信与硬连线切片，从而提升带宽利用率并绕过复杂路由仲裁逻辑。在Transformer基准上，相比传统基线延迟和能耗最多降低52%，并优于带宽等效的优化数据流映射方案。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3717165.title: PAC-NoC: A Hierarchical Network-on-Chip for Efficient Parallel Aggregated Communication in Transformer Accelerators

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718253.abstract: As the thermal issue in integrated chips becomes increasingly severe, thermal sign-off and thermal management become more important for performance and reliability. Thermal libraries provide an offline approach to avoid time-consuming real-time thermal simulations. However, thermal library characterization under multicorner scenarios for thermal sign-off is a computationally expensive task. This work decouples the thermal resistance of a standard cell into two components: the thermal critical transistors that dominate heat generation and dissipation, which are corner-invariant and determined by the cell topology, and the transistor thermal resistances, which are corner-dependent. Based on this insight, we propose a fast multicorner thermal library characterization methodology, which significantly enhances efficiency through the reuse of thermal-critical transistor information. The characterized thermal library can be seamlessly integrated into mature electronic design automation (EDA) toolchains, enabling rapid full-chip, standard cell-level thermal assessment in both steady-state and transient conditions, while accounting for thermal coupling and thermal relaxation effects. The proposed methodology reduces the thermal library characterization time for multicorner thermal libraries from several weeks to 1 h. The accuracy of the proposed thermal assessment methodology has been validated through finite element simulation, and its full-chip thermal evaluation speed is 3.8 times faster than HotSpot.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718253.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718253.summary_zh: 提出多角热库快速表征方法，将标准单元热阻解耦为角无关的热关键晶体管部分与角相关的晶体管热阻部分，通过复用热关键晶体管信息提升效率。表征所得热库可集成到成熟EDA工具链，支持稳态与瞬态的全芯片标准单元级热评估。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718253.title: A Fast Characterization Methodology of Multicorner Thermal Library for Thermal Signoff

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718287.abstract: Deep spiking neural networks (SNNs) have gained significant attention in the current landscape of neural computing, primarily due to their remarkable energy efficiency and capability to perform complex computational tasks. This article presents the hardware implementation of a residual SNN (RSNN) architecture featuring four layers equipped with residual connections. We propose a novel edge-based data encoding scheme to enhance RSNN’s efficiency. This encoding scheme significantly accelerates the training and inference processes by  $5.2\times $  and  $3.1\times $  on an Nvidia A100 GPU having 80 GB of memory, compared to conventional encoding schemes, rate, latency, and delta encoding on the MNIST, fashion-MNIST (FMNIST), and KMNIST datasets. Moreover, it drastically reduces memory usage and energy consumption by  $\sim \!37\times $  and  $\sim \!4.3\times $ . In addition, this article proposes two distinct hardware implementations of the proposed RSNN using an AMD VCK190 field-programmable gate array (FPGA): sequential RSNN (SRSNN) and sequential–parallel RSNN (SPRSNN). SRSNN uses  $\sim \!\!3\times $  fewer hardware resources than SPRSNN on an FPGA. In contrast, SPRSNN exhibits  $10.6\times $  and  $2\times $  lower latency and power consumption than SRSNN. The proposed FPGA-based realizations show an accuracy of 98%, 89%, and 95% on the MNIST, FMNIST, and KMNIST datasets, while reducing power consumption by  $3.2\times $ . They are at least  $3\times $  more resource efficient than contemporary SNN architectures with comparable latencies.

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718287.summary_zh: 提出带残差连接的脉冲神经网络硬件架构及基于边沿的数据编码方案，并在AMD VCK190 FPGA上实现顺序SRSNN与顺序-并行SPRSNN两种版本。报告编码方案使训练与推理分别加速5.2倍和3.1倍，内存与能耗降低约37倍和4.3倍，SRSNN资源约为SPRSNN的三分之一。

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718513.abstract: Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based acceleration for 3-D object detection has attracted significant attention due to its potential for high efficiency and low latency. However, existing fully sparse 3-D Transformer accelerators suffer from inefficient dataflows and limited parallelism, mainly caused by irregular sparsity patterns and global attention dependencies. To address these challenges, this work introduces the fully sparse Transformer pipeline (FST-PIPE). FST-PIPE adopts a hybrid-grained pipeline that integrates coarse-grained inter-layer streaming with fine-grained intra-operator parallelism, and incorporates a memory-efficient storage design to maximize parallelism and memory efficiency. FST-PIPE is enabled by restructuring global sparse attention into an axis-aligned representation through the proposed AxisFormer block, thereby enabling efficient modeling of long-range dependencies among spatially distant nonempty voxels. Furthermore, this work introduces a length-aware pipeline scheduling mechanism to address workload imbalance arising from variable sequence lengths, eliminating pipeline bubbles and sustaining high hardware utilization. Implemented on a ZCU102 FPGA, FST-PIPE achieves 42.59 frames/s with a latency of 23.48 ms and an energy efficiency of 9.5 frames/s/W, providing up to  $1.45\times $  higher throughput and around  $2\times $  better energy efficiency compared with prior FPGA-based accelerators.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718513.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3718513.title: A Fully Sparse Transformer Accelerator With Hybrid-Grained Pipeline for 3-D Object Detection

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3720317.abstract: Tensor virtual machine–versatile tensor accelerator (TVM–VTA) stack is an end-to-end deep neural network (DNN) accelerator template known for its high reconfigurability and flexibility. However, baseline TVM–VTA accelerator templates may introduce pipeline and scheduling inefficiencies. Pipelined VTA (PVTA) focuses on the specific execution bottlenecks of the TVM–VTA stack and develops a pipeline-oriented solution across microarchitecture and instruction flow. The proposed architecture redesigns the GEMM and ALU pipelines, instruction flow, LOAD module, and dual-thread dependency mechanism, while maintaining compatibility with the existing software-hardware stack. Implemented on Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA, the proposed PVTA achieves a DSP efficiency of 0.564, delivering $3.9\times $ and $2.54\times $ speedups over the original VTA on ResNet-50 and YOLOv3, with final throughputs of 29.2 and 7.25 fps, respectively. These improvements demonstrate the effectiveness of pipeline-focused optimizations in enhancing VTA’s performance for end-to-end DNN acceleration. Evaluation against representative VTA-based designs shows that PVTA attains the highest reported end-to-end speedup within the VTA framework. Compared to other leading architectures, the proposed approach achieves comparable or higher performance while preserving a high degree of flexibility, enabling VTA to evolve from a research template into a competitive, high-performance end-to-end accelerator.

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3722669.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), neural network applications demand increasingly efficient data processing. The traditional von Neumann architecture faces a growing “memory wall” bottleneck, making computing-in-memory (CIM) a highly promising solution. This brief presents a 4-Kb 10T static random access memory (SRAM)-CIM macro designed for convolutional neural networks (CNNs), featuring a charge–discharge consistency circuit based on a cascode current mirror that provides stable bias voltages for current-domain computation. The proposed architecture significantly improves the consistency and linearity of bitline charging and discharging, thereby enhancing computational accuracy. Furthermore, only four tail transistors in the 10T SRAM bit cell are used to perform computation, greatly improving throughput. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the SRAM-CIM macroachieves an energy efficiency of 26.43–68.78 TOPS/W and a throughput of 1016 GOPS. With four-bit signed input and four-bit unsigned weight precision, the circuit achieves estimated inference accuracies of 93.4% on the MNIST dataset and 81.6% on the CIFAR-10 dataset.

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3722669.title: 28-nm High-Consistency SRAM-CIM Macro With Cascode Current Mirror for Convolutional Neural Networks

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3722763.abstract: Multiprecision multiply-accumulate (MAC) units from INT2 to FP32 are increasingly needed on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). However, the existing processing element (PE) designs mostly follow application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC)-oriented composition strategies. Their alignment and selection networks map to lookup table (LUT)-based multiplexing logic and incur rapidly increasing delay on FPGA platforms. We perform a controlled study of composition depth on three Xilinx platforms, spanning the Zynq-7000, Kintex UltraScale+, and Zynq UltraScale+ families. Each added composition layer incurs a steady frequency penalty, and four or more layers lose roughly half of the full-width maximum frequency. Based on this result, we propose hybrid high-precision composition (HHPC). The HHPC bounds in-array composition to a fixed depth. It moves residual high-precision assembly to postarray logic or inter-PE cooperation. It also preserves a fixed control structure across all modes. Based on HHPC, we implement a reconfigurable PE that supports INT2, INT4, INT8, FP16, and FP32 in a unified pipeline. FP32 is supported in two modes. A single PE produces one result every three cycles. A cooperative 3-PE tile sustains one FP32 MAC per cycle. On ZCU102, the proposed design achieves up to 310.60 GOPS/W for INT2 and 3.24 GFLOPS/W for FP32. It delivers up to $3.0\times $ higher energy efficiency than a comparable reconfigurable multiprecision PE with the same precision coverage.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3722763.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3722763.summary_zh: 针对FPGA上INT2至FP32多精度MAC单元，研究组合深度对频率的影响并提出混合高精度组合（HHPC）策略，将阵列内组合限制在固定深度、把剩余高精度装配移至阵列后逻辑或PE间协作。基于HHPC实现统一流水线可重构PE，支持INT2/INT4/INT8/FP16/FP32，摘要片段称单PE每三周期产出一个FP32结果，但给定片段未披露完整PPA对比数据。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3722763.title: A Low-Bit-First Multiprecision Processing Element for Energy-Efficient FPGA Implementation

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3729639.abstract: Digital power control applications impose stringent real-time computational demands, particularly for trigonometric operations in closed-loop systems. To address this challenge, we propose a domain-specific RISC-V controller for digital power (DSRVC-DP), a customized controller based on the tinyriscv open-source processor. The design extends the RISC-V instruction set with hardware-accelerated trigonometric operations via a memoized CORDIC unit, which exploits data reuse to eliminate redundant iterations. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements over DSP and ARM controllers. Single-angle evaluation and trigonometric-table generation are significantly accelerated, and the interrupt service routine (ISR) execution time in closed-loop control is reduced by 48% and 27% in inverter control, and by 36% and 11% in the phase-locked-loop (PLL) applications, respectively. These results confirm DSRVC-DP’s effectiveness in enhancing real-time performance for digital power control.

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3729757.abstract: This article proposes a nonreturn-to-zero (NRZ)/PAM-4 dual-mode transmitter for low-power double data rate (LPDDR) memory interfaces that employs a transmitter-interleaving (TI) technique to enhance power efficiency while maintaining high-speed signaling capability. Instead of separate data and clock paths in the conventional dual-mode transmitters, the proposed architecture inserts clock-controlled NMOS switches into the low-voltage swing-terminated logic (LVSTL) output driver structure, thereby merging the serialization path with the driver stage. This structural integration eliminates the need for a dedicated high-speed serializer and reduces switching activity in the driver block. A prior TI driver-based transmitter requires a clock bootstrapping circuit and typically does not support ZQ calibration, resulting in impedance mismatch. In contrast, this work removes the bootstrapping circuit and adopts a dual-mode ZQ calibration scheme that maintains constant output impedance across both NRZ and PAM-4 modes. A prototype chip is fabricated in a 1-poly 10-metal (1P10LM) 28-nm CMOS process. Measured results demonstrate that the proposed transmitter consumes 10.82 mW while transmitting 11-Gb/s PAM-4 data, achieving an energy efficiency of 0.98-pJ/b, confirming that the proposed structure is highly suitable for LPDDR.

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3729757.title: An NRZ/PAM-4 Dual-Mode Transmitter Using Tx-Interleaving Technique for Low-Power DRAM Interfaces

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3731472.abstract: Floating-point computing-in-memory (FP-CIM) macros typically suffer from prohibitive area and power overheads due to the complexity of alignment logic. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel FP-CIM macro that integrates two key in-memory operations: shifting-in-memory exponent normalization (SIMENP) and shifting-in-memory mantissa alignment (SIMMAP). SIMENP enables in-array exponent shifting using the proposed 9T bitcell, thereby eliminating redundant processing latency. For mantissa alignment, a midrange-based subtraction-shifting scheme is implemented using the proposed 10T bitcell, which obviates the need for dedicated shift registers while halving the clock cycles required for data shifting. The proposed macro is designed and simulated in a 28-nm CMOS process with a 36-kB capacity. Simulation results demonstrate an energy efficiency of 11.63 TFLOPS/W at 150 MHz under a 0.55 V supply. Compared to state-of-the-art subtractor-based FP-CIM architectures and D flip-flop (DFF) combined schemes, the proposed design reduces the shifting-logic area by 45.7%, while also reducing the number of cycles required for mantissa alignment by 50%.
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3731472.journal: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3731472.summary_zh: 提出28nm浮点存内计算宏，利用9T与10T位单元实现阵列内指数归一化移位和基于指数中值的尾数对齐移位，省去专用移位寄存器。仿真显示36kB容量下150MHz、0.55V时能效11.63 TFLOPS/W，移位逻辑面积减少45.7%，尾数对齐周期数减半。
doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3731472.title: A 28-nm Floating-Point SRAM-CIM Macro With In-Array Shifting for Exponent Normalization and Mantissa Alignment Based on Exponent Midrange

doi:10.1109/tvlsi.2026.3732384.abstract: The binarized neural networks (BNNs) significantly reduce arithmetic and storage costs for edge inference, but repeated bitwise accumulation and memory access still limit system energy efficiency. This article presents leak-computing-in-memory (CIM), a $256\times 64$ static random access memory (SRAM)-based voltage-mode CIM macro that exploits the subthreshold leakage of off -state transistors as ultrahigh-impedance pseudo-resistors for low-energy analog accumulation. Unlike charge-sharing CIMs, the proposed scheme maintains a wide read-bitline (RBL) dynamic range while strongly suppressing the shoot-through current that typically limits voltage-mode operation. To compensate for the process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity of leakage-based pull-up and pull-down paths, the leak-CIM employs a postfabrication N-well bias calibration scheme that restores their resistance balance. The postlayout simulations show that the calibrated macro maintains a normalized mean-squared error below $1.12\times 10^{-2}$ across 40 global PVT conditions. Fabricated in a 22-nm bulk-CMOS process, the macro achieves up to 1799 TOPS/W and 31.67 TOPS/mm 2 across measured operating points. When the measured ADC characteristics are incorporated into a BNN inference model, leak-CIM attains 98.15% accuracy on MNIST and 86.04% on CIFAR-10.

doi:10.1109/vlsitechnologyandcir65830.20.abstract: This work presents a neural-network augmented cryo-CMOS readout IC for superconducting quantum computing. With the FCNN-based qubit state detector, this IC achieves the ability of real-time qubit readout drift monitoring and adaptive drift mitigation. Adopting the FIR-DSM-based stimulus TX technique, the measured TX power is 2.6mW, which is $>1.9 \mathrm{x}$ lower than prior designs. Quadrature digital-IF reflected RX is implemented with stimulus pulses synthesis and reflected signal processing, resulting in a fully-functional readout IC with a lowest power of 10.3mW. Verification with a transmon qubit at 4K, this IC achieves a readout fidelity up to 95.6%.

doi:10.1109/vlsitechnologyandcir65830.20.abstract: Artificial intelligence is driving exponential growth in computation, data transfer, and energy consumption. As model sizes surpass the trillion-parameter threshold and reasoning workloads increase demands on bandwidth and latency, memory has emerged as the central constraint for advanced AI systems rather than compute resources. Meeting these exponential requirements necessitates coordinated advancements in memory technologies—such as DRAM and NAND, high-bandwidth memory, and packaging solutions including hybrid bonding, fine-pitch die-to-die interconnects, and vertically stacked memory architectures. Breakthroughs in materials science, sophisticated physics-based modeling, wafer bonding, and advanced metrology solutions are essential for rapid progress. The integration of emerging non-volatile memories and CXL-enabled expansion frameworks further supports heterogeneous and composable memory systems tailored for large-scale AI. This work summarizes key device, packaging, energy-efficiency, and memory innovations needed for future AI workloads.

doi:10.1109/vlsitechnologyandcir65830.20.abstract: Vertical Stacked DRAM (VS-DRAM) has emerged as a promising candidate to extend DRAM generations beyond the 10 nm node, leveraging cell stacking similar to V-NAND. Demonstrating reliable device operation at higher tiers is crucial to ensuring its competitiveness. For the first time, this paper presents experimental results of a 16-tier VS-DRAM structure. The study integrates Gate-All-Around (GAA) type cell transistors (CTR) and horizontal storage capacitors (CAP) and compares these results with conventional DRAM. Additionally, a core/peri ($\mathrm{C} / \mathrm{P}$) device is fabricated on a separate wafer and its backside is bonded to the cell wafer, enabling the implementation of Peri-on-Cell architecture. The findings highlight the potential of VS-DRAM and pave the way for future DRAM innovations.
