This design enables an efficient execution pipeline and overlaps on-chip computation with memory access. Evaluations show that our work is the first to outperform dense matrix multiplication on modern GPUs equipped with high-bandwidth memory (HBM). It achieves up to 1.64× kernel-level speedup over SpInfer (EuroSys'25, Best paper) and up to 1.41× end-to-end speedups over FlashLLM (VLDB'24). Our source code: https://github.com/moui0/cudac.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804227.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804227.summary_zh: 研究面向LLM中等非结构化稀疏权重的GPU推理方法，提出三层矩阵存储格式与联合使用稀疏张量核和CUDA核的SpMM内核。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804227.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804228.abstract: Log schema extraction, the process of deriving human-readable templates that support clear log understanding from massive volumes of log data, is fundamental for automated debugging and performance analysis across modern Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tool chains. The challenge is amplified in advanced design flows, where logs interweave command scripts, multi-stage progress reports, timing updates, and deeply nested performance tables, rendering manual regular-expression design brittle and nonscalable to evolving tool versions. We introduce SchemaCoder, a fully-automated LLM-driven schema extraction framework that constructs structured log schemas by synthesizing reusable parser code, enabling robust handling of arbitrary unstructured log files and complex EDA tool logs without manual regular-expression design. At its core, SchemaCoder uses a novel Question-Tree (Q-Tree) pattern code generation process to identify pattern codes and utilizes the extracted raw contents to drive a textual residual evolutionary optimizer in the inner loop without relying on a gold labeled dataset. In the outer loop, a residual Q-Tree boosting mechanism identifies additional pattern codes and iteratively refines the parser code. On EDA tool logs from OpenROAD and commercial tools, the structured log schema generated by SchemaCoder enables an average 11.7% improvement in agentic EDA tool log analysis QA tasks (pass@1) over a strong commercial baseline. SchemaCoder also achieves up to 3.3% improvement in the average scores and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in 9 of 14 applications on LogHub-2.0. The source code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/NVlabs/SchemaCoder.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804228.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804228.summary_zh: 提出SchemaCoder，用LLM驱动的Q-Tree模式代码生成与残差进化优化自动提取日志模式，面向EDA工具链日志解析。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804228.title: SchemaCoder: Automatic Log Schema Extraction Coder with Residual Q-Tree Boosting

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804229.abstract: Advanced 3D and 3.5D IC packaging significantly improves integration density but elevates thermal management challenges due to cross-layer heat coupling and complex cooling structures. Traditional solvers deliver high fidelity but are too slow for iterative design flows, while existing learning-based methods either fail to capture inter-die thermal coupling or treat cooling structures as static components, limiting their applicability in real packaging co-design scenarios. In this work, we introduce COOL, a cooling-aware point transformer framework that represents heterogeneous assemblies (dies, interposers, TIMs, heat spreaders) as annotated 3D point clouds embedding geometric, material and power attributes. COOL explicitly encodes geometric boundaries and cooling structures, and introduces a physics-informed boundary condition (PI-BC) loss to enforce thermal consistency at material interfaces and cooling boundaries. Extensive experiments demonstrate that COOL achieves a remarkable 2.4\% NMAE on our constructed benchmark of multi-package thermal designs, substantially outperforming existing learning-based approaches while providing over 15.7x speedup compared to commercial FEM solvers.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804229.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804229.summary_zh: 提出COOL，用冷却感知点变换器对3D/3.5D IC封装进行热预测，报告2.4% NMAE及相对商业FEM求解器15.7倍加速。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804229.title: COOL: A Cooling-Aware Point Transformer Framework for Thermal Prediction in Advanced 3D/3.5D IC Packaging

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804230.abstract: Weights in neural networks (NNs) are signed. Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM), though a promising computing in-memory (CiM) for NN acceleration, is inherently unipolar as the conductance can only be positive, making it challenging to represent signed weights. Existing mainstream solutions utilize a differential pair of RRAM cells for representing a signed weight, which double the array size and significantly increase peripheral circuit cost, limiting the scalability and energy efficiency of CiM accelerators. In this work, instead of assigning a specific sign to each weight, we treat each column of the CiM crossbar as a unit and assign an identical sign to the entire column. To do this, we propose a Sign-Align Training and Mapping (SATM) framework that regularizes the network during training so that all weights mapped to the same column of a CiM crossbar share an identical sign. A Per-column Sign Register (PSR) is added to the array's periphery to store the learned 1-bit sign configuration for each respective column. The experimental results show that the proposed SATM achieves up to 49.3% reduction in area overhead and up to 60.7% reduction in energy consumption for AlexNet, ResNet18, VGG16, ResNet50, and vision transformer models compared to differential-pair implementations.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804230.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804230.summary_zh: 提出按列符号对齐的训练与映射框架，在RRAM存内计算阵列外围加每列符号寄存器以表示有符号权重，报告面积与能耗降低。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804230.title: Signing Crossbar Columns Instead of Neural Network Weights in Compute-in-Memory Accelerators

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804231.abstract: Hardware design verification is essential for ensuring the functional correctness of electronic designs. Recent advances have explored using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate hardware test-bench synthesis. However, existing approaches primarily target single hardware modules and often fail to generalize to complex, system-level designs. As design complexity increases, both the LLM-generated testbench and the reference design are more likely to exhibit correlated or compensating errors, often producing false-positive outcomes that obscure true functional violations. To tackle these challenges, we propose ReflectBench, an agentic framework for automated system-level hardware design verification with logic analysis, consensus-based validation, feedback self-reflection, and testbench self-correction. To further minimize manual effort in preparing data, we devise Self-Reflective Domain Knowledge Mining, an automated approach for constructing an effective retrieval database aligned with hardware semantics. We also develop ReflectVDB, a benchmark consisting of 53 system-level hardware designs for evaluating LLM-based verification frameworks. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms SOTA framework ConfiBench on both ReflectVDB and AutoBench datasets, achieving 7.6% and 4.5% improvement in terms of testbench generation success rate, and 3.8% and 1.2% improvement in terms of coverage rate. The framework and ReflectVDB benchmark are open-sourced at https://gitee.com/sdu-aes-lab/reflectbench.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804231.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804231.summary_zh: 提出ReflectBench，一个面向系统级硬件设计验证的智能体框架，结合逻辑分析、共识验证、反馈自反思与测试平台自纠正，并构建含53个系统级硬件设计的ReflectVDB基准。摘要片段未披露完整实验数值。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804231.title: ReflectBench: An Agentic Framework for Generating System-Level Design Testbench via Consensus and Reflection

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804232.abstract: Physical design is a critical step in the electronic design automation (EDA) process, where the gate-level netlist from logic synthesis is converted into a GDS-II file. Recently, AI methods have been increasingly employed to address challenges in physical design. This paper proposes a new paradigm that integrates routing metric evaluation and optimization on chip layouts, forming a "Generate-Evaluate-Optimize -Generate" (GEOG) closed-loop. In our experiments, the pre-routing generation model achieves a mean relative error (MRE) of only 1%, with a mean absolute error (MAE) below one movement unit. Post-processing reduces both MRE and MAE to zero while ensuring connectivity. The evaluation model performs comparably to iSTA on the test set, with a 336× speedup. Furthermore, the optimization strategy effectively improves wirelength, delay, slew, R, and C by 10.49%, 13.03%, 14.85%, 10.51%, and 6.46%, respectively, and produces routing results superior to commercial tools in key metrics.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804232.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804232.summary_zh: 提出芯片布局预训练范式，将布线度量评估与优化集成为生成-评估-优化-再生成的闭环，预布线生成模型MRE约1%，评估模型相对iSTA有336倍加速，优化使线长、延迟、转换、R、C分别改善10.49%、13.03%、14.85%、10.51%、6.46%。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804232.title: iPCL-M: Pre-training of Chip Layout for Metrics Evaluation and Optimization

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804233.abstract: 3D In-memory Computing (IMC) chips, with high density and bandwidth, offer a promising solution for AI workloads but suffer from thermal instability, which degrades weight precision and system throughput. This work proposes a cross-layer thermal stability strategy (TSS) and validates it on a 3D eFlash analog IMC prototype with hybrid bonding, integrating a 12nm logic die and a 28nm eFlash die (36MB). TSS consists of: (1) a physics-guided thermal model achieving a kullback-leibler divergence of 0.088; (2) a temperature-insensitive differential programming (TIDP) scheme that stabilizes weights from -30°C to 60°C; and (3) an adaptive temperature calibration (ATC) algorithm that reduces output error standard deviation by 60.7%. With TSS, ResNet-18 and DCCRN maintain robust inference on the 3D eFlash IMC SoC across -15°C to 75°C with less than 10% degradation in end-to-end task accuracy. This is the first demonstration of thermally resilient analog IMC on a commercial-grade 3D SoC, paving the way for reliable AI deployment under dynamic thermal conditions.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804233.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804233.summary_zh: 在12nm/28nm混合键合晶圆对晶圆3D集成eFlash模拟存内计算SoC上提出跨层热稳定策略，含物理引导热模型、温度不敏感差分编程与自适应温度校准。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804233.title: Thermal Stability Strategy for a 12nm/28nm Hybrid-Bonding Wafer-on-Wafer 3D-Integrated eFlash In-Memory Computing SoC

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804234.abstract: Flash wear raises raw bit error rate (RBER), limiting SSD lifetime by TBW or P/E cycles. We present SSD Reforge, which dynamically strengthens protection near end-of-life by adding intra-device parity, allowing more lifetime. To handle inter-block reliability heterogeneity, we build an RBER-based error-probability model and derive parity stripe grouping as a combinatorial optimization problem. We design Reliability-Aware Striping (RAS) for efficient grouping and Stripe UPER Leveling (SUPERL) to sustain RAS during subsequent writes. Implemented in FEMU and evaluated with real I/O traces, SSD Reforge increases user TBW by up to 40% on average versus traditional mode at the lifetime limit, significantly extending SSD lifespan.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804234.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804234.summary_zh: 研究SSD闪存磨损下的动态奇偶校验管理与寿命延长。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804234.title: SSD Reforge: Dynamic Parity Management to Extend SSD Lifetime under Aging

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804235.abstract: Bird's-eye-view (BEV) fusion of multi-modal sensor data is a leading approach for high-performance 3D object detection. However, state-of-the-art models rarely exceed 10 FPS even on powerful GPUs, limiting their use in real-time applications. In this paper, we present a neural architecture search (NAS) framework that identifies models achieving both high accuracy and real-time inference. The search space is explicitly designed with hardware constraints to balance accuracy and computational efficiency on resource-limited platforms. To better align LiDAR and camera features in the BEV conversion module, we introduce a lightweight depth estimation network and a LiDAR-camera cross-attention mechanism that enhances detection accuracy with minimal overhead. On the challenging nuScenes benchmark, our model achieves 70.1% mAP, which represents a 2.3% point improvement over the baseline model, while running at 35.6 FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, demonstrating its suitability for real-time autonomous driving.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804235.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804235.summary_zh: 提出面向BEV三维目标检测的硬件感知神经架构搜索。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804235.title: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Real-Time BEV-Based 3D Object Detection

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804236.abstract: General matrix-matrix multiplication (GEMM) remains the dominant computational kernel in transformer-based large language model (LLM) inference. However, large-scale matrices with irregular sparsity limit energy efficiency by hindering regular data access and efficient processing element (PE)-array execution. To address this challenge, we present PEACE, an algorithm-hardware co-design for energy-aware compressed GEMM at the PE-array granularity. PEACE-Alg exploits column-wise energy distribution to restructure large matrices into compressed formats aligned with hardware execution. To support PEACE-Alg, we design PEACE-Hw, which integrates RISC-V ISA extensions, metadata-guided operand scheduling, a reconfigurable systolic PE array, and dedicated partial-sum accumulation support. Experimental results show that PEACE occupies 2.705 mm2 in a 14 nm ASIC, achieves 1.60×-1.67× speedup over a RISC-V core baseline across 14 transformer-based LLMs. Compared with state-of-the-art designs, PEACE achieves 4.4× PE density, 1.79× average speedup, and 2.53× energy efficiency.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804236.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804236.summary_zh: 提出PEACE算法-硬件协同设计，含RISC-V ISA扩展、可重构脉动PE阵列与部分和累加支持，实现压缩GEMM加速。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804236.title: PEACE: Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design for PE-Granular Energy-Aware Compressed GEMM Acceleration

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804237.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise exceptional energy efficiency for neuromorphic computing through event-driven processing. However, unlocking their full potential requires navigating a complex, strongly coupled design space of network topology and temporal neural encoding. Existing SNN Neural Architecture Search (NAS) frameworks typically decouple these dimensions, focusing exclusively on topology search while relying on manual, fixed encoding schemes. This limitation leaves a vast portion of the design space unexplored, resulting in sub-optimal energy-accuracy tradeoffs. To bridge this gap, we present ACE-NAS, the first zero-cost NAS framework that automates the co-design of SNN architecture and encoding mechanisms. Addressing the challenge of "encoding-blind" proxies, we introduce Jacob_cov, a novel Jacobian-based spectral metric that efficiently quantifies the temporal discriminability of different encoding schemes without training. ACE-NAS integrates Jacob_cov with structural proxies (ZiCo) into a hardware-aware, multi-objective evolutionary search strategy. On CIFAR-10, ACE-NAS achieves 92.95% accuracy, effectively identifying Pareto-optimal designs that balance high performance with minimal spike activity. By automating the joint optimization of structure and dynamics, ACE-NAS delivers an orders-of-magnitude reduction compared to standard training-based NAS and a 7× speedup over state-of-the-art efficient SNN-NAS methods (e.g., AutoSNN).
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804237.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804237.summary_zh: 提出面向脉冲神经网络的零成本架构与编码协同搜索框架。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804237.title: ACE-NAS: A Zero-Cost NAS Framework for Co-Design of Architecture and Encoding in Spiking Neural Networks

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804238.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models build a token-domain robot control paradigm, yet suffer from low speed. Speculative Decoding (SD) is an optimization strategy that can boost inference speed. Two key issues emerge when integrating VLA and SD: first, SD relies on re-inference to address token errors, which is computationally expensive; second, to mitigate token errors, the acceptance threshold in SD requires careful adjustment. Existing works fail to address the above two issues effectively. Meanwhile, as the bridge between AI and the physical world, existing embodied intelligence has overlooked the application of robotic kinematics. To address these issues, we innovatively combine token-domain VLA models with kinematic-domain prediction for SD, proposing a kinematic-rectified SD framework named KERV. We employ a kinematics-based Kalman Filter to predict actions and compensate for SD errors, avoiding costly re-inference. Moreover, we design a kinematics-based adjustment strategy to dynamically rectify the acceptance threshold, addressing the difficulty of threshold determination. Experimental results across diverse tasks and environments demonstrate that KERV achieves 27%~37% acceleration with nearly no Success Rate loss.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804238.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804238.summary_zh: 提出面向具身VLA模型的运动学校正推测解码框架。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804238.title: KERV: Kinematic-Rectified Speculative Decoding for Embodied VLA Models

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804239.abstract: Real-time thermal monitoring of 3D integrated circuits confronts a fundamental observability crisis: reconstructing high-resolution volumetric thermal fields from sparse, heterogeneous on-chip observations. We demonstrate that existing single-modality approaches are physically insufficient—performance counters capture heat generation but they are blind to thermal transport, while sparse thermal sensors capture local states and provide thermal responses, but lack spatial coverage. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Physics-Informed 3D Conditional Diffusion Architecture (PI-3D-CD) which synergistically fuses these complementary modalities, treating thermal reconstruction as a constrained inference problem over the heat equation. Our 3D architecture explicitly models vertical inter-layer coupling, reducing estimation error by over 94% (0.48 K vs. 13.08 K RMSE) compared to single-source baselines. Furthermore, by leveraging deterministic sampling, we accelerate inference 158× over finite-element simulation (0.93s vs. 147.4s) while maintaining high physical fidelity (R2 > 0.98). This work establishes a new, observability-driven paradigm for thermal monitoring, enabling practical closed-loop dynamic thermal management for next-generation 3D integrated circuits.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804239.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804239.summary_zh: 提出物理信息扩散模型从稀疏片上观测重建三维集成电路热场。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804239.title: Seeing Through Silicon: Multimodal Thermal Reconstruction via Physics-Informed Diffusion

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804300.abstract: Counter-based stochastic computing (CBSC) utilizes simple counting logic to realize multiplication. Inspired by CBSC, this paper proposes the ALOHA architecture that significantly reduces the computing latency and stochastic number generation (SNG) overhead. Specifically, ALOHA incorporates three key innovations, including input scaling, bit-reversal counter-based SNG, and sequence-aware optimization schemes. Experimental results show that the ALOHA multiplier significantly outperforms state-of-the-art CBSC designs in terms of accuracy, area and power consumption with reduced sequence length. In CNN and Transformer inference, ALOHA matches the accuracy of prior FSM-based multipliers while reducing area and energy.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804300.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804300.summary_zh: 提出基于Hamersley序列的计数器随机计算架构ALOHA，含输入缩放、位反转SNG与序列感知优化。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804300.title: ALOHA: Area-efficient and Low-power StOchastic Computing with HAmmersley Sequences

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804301.abstract: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) suffers from substantial performance overhead in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE)-based privacy-preserving computing, as encryption obscures matrix sparsity and forces dense computation. To overcome this limitation, we introduce SparseE, a hardware-software co-design framework that enables sparsity-aware SpMM under FHE. Our key contribution is a novel protocol that transforms SpMM into a secure Scatter-Gather-Apply workflow, where a homomorphic permutation network securely gathers data using encrypted indices. This approach ensures computational cost scales with the number of non-zero elements while fully preserving sparsity pattern confidentiality. To further boost performance, we co-design a dedicated accelerator featuring a Homomorphic Permutation Engine based on a hardware-efficient Benes topology—implemented as a Radix-2 Single-Delay Feedback pipeline of HSwitch units—to alleviate on-chip bandwidth constraints. In tandem, a Homomorphic Expansion Engine performs real-time decompression of selector ciphertexts, effectively mitigating storage bottlenecks. Extensive experiments across four representative applications show that SparseE achieves speedups ranging from 2.7× to 192.2×, and energy reductions from 15.5× to 251.5× over state-of-the-art hardware accelerators. The source code for this project is publicly available at https://github.com/yuntao-wei/SparseE.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804301.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804301.summary_zh: 提出FHE下稀疏矩阵乘的软硬件协同设计，含基于Benes拓扑的同态置换引擎与同态扩展引擎加速器。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804301.title: SparseE: Unlocking Sparsities in Encrypted Sparse Matrix Multiplication via Hardware-Software Co-Design

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804302.abstract: Performing Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) on large-scale vector datasets is essential for AI applications. Graph-based ANNS demonstrates superior performance and accuracy, positioning itself as a leading approach within the ANNS landscape. However, its inherent reliance on random data access mandates a memory-centric deployment strategy, which, in turn, poses significant scalability challenges. Recent advancements in Compute eXpress Link (CXL) technologies, known for their high-bandwidth memory extension capabilities, offer a critical opportunity to enhance the scalability of graph-based ANNS. Nonetheless, the implications of the CXL-extended memory architecture when applied to graph-based ANNS remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we present a CXL-Oriented Graph-based ANNS (COGA) system to achieve scalable, high-speed ANNS for extensive datasets. Our key observation is that the search pipeline can be enhanced through a CXL-tailored priority queue that maximizes CXL bandwidth utilization while bridging the latency gap. Furthermore, we propose a tiered data layout and placement strategy that leverages queue hints to facilitate speculative access to index data. Evaluation results show that our system achieves a speedup of 2.8–4.5× compared to existing CXL-based approaches.

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804302.summary_zh: 提出基于CXL分层数据放置的可扩展图ANNS系统。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804302.title: TierANNS: Scalable Graph-based ANNS with CXL-enabled Tiered Data Placement

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804303.abstract: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained edge devices is a critical but challenging task, primarily due to the prohibitive memory and computational costs of backpropagation. While forward-only optimizers like MeZO mitigate these costs by eliminating the backward pass, they often suffer from slow and unstable convergence, particularly on loss landscapes with heterogeneous curvature. To address this limitation, we introduce PeFoo, a general framework for preconditioner enhanced forward only optimizer. PeFoo integrates a carefully designed preconditioning strategy into the forward-only paradigm, corrects a fundamental source of bias and instability present in prior work HiZOO. Furthermore, to counteract the memory overhead introduced by the preconditioner itself, we propose PeFoo-L, which employs a layer-wise update strategy. This approach constrains preconditioner storage and weight updates to a single layer per iteration, reducing the overall memory footprint and data traffic. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our framework. In the OPT-1.3B model, PeFoo substantially exceeds the accuracy of leading zeroth-order methods MeZO and HiZOO by 2.7% and 2.1%, respectively. Furthermore, PeFoo-L achieves a memory footprint reduction of over 2.73× and 1.75× compared to Adam and HiZOO, while delivering faster convergence speed compared to MeZO and HiZOO.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804303.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804303.summary_zh: 提出预条件前向优化器框架以支持边缘设备LLM微调。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804303.title: PeFoo-L: A General Framework for Preconditioned Forward-Only Optimizer Enabling LLM Fine-tuning on the Edge

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804304.abstract: In deep networks, operations such as ReLU and hardware-driven clamping often cause activations to accumulate near the edges of the distribution, leading to biased clustering and suboptimal quantization in existing nonlinear (NL) quantization methods. This paper introduces Boundary Suppressed K-Means Quantization (BS-KMQ), a novel NL quantization approach designed to reduce the resolution requirements of analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) in in-memory computing (IMC) systems. By suppressing boundary outliers before clustering, BS-KMQ achieves more balanced and informative NL quantization levels. The resulting NL references are implemented using a reconfigurable in-memory NL-ADC, achieving a 7× area improvement over prior NL-ADC designs. When evaluated on ResNet-18, VGG-16, Inception-V3, and DistilBERT, BS-KMQ achieves at least 3× lower quantization error compared to linear, Lloyd-Max, cumulative distribution function (CDF), and K-means methods. It also improves post-training quantization accuracy by up to 66.8%, 25.4%, 66.6%, and 67.7%, respectively, compared to linear quantization. After low-bit fine-tuning, BS-KMQ maintains competitive accuracy with significantly fewer NL-ADC levels (3/3/4/4b). System-level simulations on ResNet-18 (6/2/3b) demonstrate up to a 4× speedup and 24× energy efficiency improvement over existing IMC accelerators.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804304.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804304.summary_zh: 提出边界抑制K-Means量化（BS-KMQ）及可重构存内非线性ADC，以降低存内计算系统的ADC分辨率需求，并报告相比先前NL-ADC设计7倍面积改进。在ResNet-18、VGG-16、Inception-V3和DistilBERT上量化误差至少降低3倍，线性量化后训练精度最高提升66.8%等；摘要片段未披露完整低比特微调结果。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804304.title: In-Memory ADC-Based Nonlinear Activation Quantization for Efficient In-Memory Computing

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804305.abstract: With the rapidly growing demand of cloud computing and large-scale AI models, many-core systems are facing challenges of longer global interconnect distances in Network-on-Chip (NoC). Though conventional 2D NoCs can apply relative high metal layer for global routing, the extensive repeater insertion for long-distance transmission results in a large number of stacked vias, leading to performance degradation. Targeting high-performance CPU clusters at 3nm node, this work adopts a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) framework to evaluate long-distance NoC interconnects across four implementation schemes: conventional frontside 2D (F2D), frontside 3D (F3D) with M3D integration, F2D with backside power delivery network (BSPDN), and backside 2D (B2D) leveraging wafer backside signal routing & PDN. Based on post-layout extraction of the ARM Neoverse CSS N2 computing tile, we incorporate realistic PDN characteristics, technology-dependent RC modeling, and IR-drop-aware circuit simulation. Results show that F3D and B2D reduce delay by 53% and 68%, and energy-delay product (EDP) by 32% and 63%, respectively, compared with F2D. F2D-BSPDN achieves performance comparable to F3D. System-level NoC evaluations further demonstrate that F3D/B2D enable 2.1×/3.1× feasible link frequencies of F2D, and lower average NoC latency of F2D by 23%/35%. The DTCO analysis indicates that while F2D remains adequate for small cores (Cortex-A76), B2D is the optimal choice for mid-core (Cortex-A720, X4) and large-core (Cortex-X925, CSS N2) clusters, with F3D providing secondary benefits through repeater relocation. These findings identify backside interconnect as a momentous technology for ultra-large many-core processors.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804305.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804305.summary_zh: 针对3nm高性能CPU簇的NoC长距离互连，采用DTCO框架比较前side 2D、M3D前side 3D、BSPDN及背面2D四种方案，基于ARM Neoverse CSS N2计算瓦片的后布局提取与IR-drop感知仿真。报告F3D和B2D相比F2D分别降低延迟53%和68%、EDP 32%和63%。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804305.title: Design Technology Co-optimization for Network on Chip in High Performance CPUs at 3nm node using Monolithic 3D and Backside Interconnect Technologies

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804306.abstract: Merkle tree, as a fundamental cryptographic primitive for ensuring user privacy, play a critical role in zero-knowledge proof systems (ZKPs). However, its construction involves numerous computationally intensive Poseidon hashes, creating the primary computational bottleneck in ZKP systems. To address this challenge, we propose PhotoMT, the first photonic-electronic collaborative merkle tree engine. PhotoMT leverages the photonic microring resonator (MR) array for intensive matrix-vector multiplications to boost throughput and energy efficiency, while digital circuits handle control-intensive tasks. Furthermore, PhotoMT incorporates a multi-subtree interleaved execution strategy and an S-BOX bypass computation queue, which together improve hardware utilization and reduce memory overhead. The experiments reveal that PhotoMT boosts throughput by 18.8–20.5× over state-of-the-art AISC-based designs, achieving an energy efficiency gain of 3–5 orders of magnitude against the CPU baseline.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804306.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804306.summary_zh: 提出光子-电子协同Merkle树引擎PhotoMT，用微环谐振器阵列加速Poseidon哈希矩阵向量乘，数字电路负责控制密集型任务，并设计多子树交错执行与S-BOX旁路队列。实验报告相比先进ASIC设计吞吐提升18.8–20.5倍，能效较CPU基线提升3–5个数量级。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804306.title: PhotoMT : Accelerating Zero-Knowledge Proofs with a Photonic-Electronic Merkle Tree Engine

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804307.abstract: Databases utilizing fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) are the leading approach to preserving privacy for outsourced data. However, each query necessitates a full scan of all encrypted entries, imposing severe limitations on data access and processing efficiency. To address this bottleneck, we propose PIMA-SecDB, a processing-in-memory (PIM) architecture for FHE-based databases designed through rigorous hardware-software co-design. PIMA-SecDB features a three-tier hierarchical structure: the DIMM-level aggregation module, the x8 chip level with in-memory functional units, and the bank group level for data storage—enabling high intra-module bandwidth and parallelism for efficient in-situ processing. Moreover, we have developed a set of data management mechanisms to adapt to the parallel computing capabilities of PIMA-SecDB and a quantitative approach for selecting PIM-compatible encryption parameters to reduce computational load and data footprint. The experiment shows that PIMA-SecDB offers performance enhancements from 2.14 to 7.89× compared to existing FHE accelerators.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804307.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804307.summary_zh: 提出面向FHE数据库的存内处理架构PIMA-SecDB，采用DIMM级、x8芯片级与bank group级三层结构及存内功能单元，并配套数据管理与加密参数选择机制。实验报告相比现有FHE加速器获得2.14–7.89倍性能提升。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804307.title: PIMA-SecDB: Processing-in-memory Acceleration for Fully Homomorphic Encryption Databases

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804308.abstract: This paper presents an analytical global placement framework that concurrently integrates PDN optimization, effectively addressing both global and local IR-drop challenges. To enable accurate and efficient voltage drop estimation, we implement a fast, GPU-accelerated IR-drop analysis engine based on Modified Nodal Analysis (MNA). For PDN optimization, we introduce an iterative strategy that enhances power delivery robustness by inserting additional power delivery paths to reduce global IR-drop. To further address localized IR-drop issues, we propose a novel density control mechanism that constrains cell placement based on the maximum tolerable power load at each PDN node, as determined by IR-drop severity. Experimental results show that the proposed methodology significantly reduces IR-drop violations without incurring additional wirelength, runtime, or routability overhead compared to state-of-the-art IR-drop-aware placement techniques.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804308.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804308.summary_zh: 提出同时集成PDN优化的解析式全局布局框架，用基于MNA的GPU加速IR-drop分析引擎，并通过迭代插入供电路径与基于节点功率负载的密度控制缓解全局和局部IR-drop。报告在不增加线长、运行时间或可布线性开销的情况下显著减少IR-drop违例。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804308.title: IR-Drop Aware Global Placement with PDN Optimization and GPU-Accelerated Analysis for Mitigating Global and Local IR-Drop

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804309.abstract: RRAM-based in-memory computing (IMC) offers high energy efficiency but suffers from conductance drift that severely degrades long-term accuracy. Existing approaches including retraining, noise-aware training, and Batch Normalization (BN)-based calibration either require RRAM rewriting, demand large storage overhead, or rely on online correction. We propose VeRA+, a lightweight drift compensation framework that reuses shared projection matrices and introduces only two compact drift-specific vectors per drift level. A drift-aware scheduling algorithm offline-trains a small set of VeRA+ parameters and selects the appropriate set over time without any on-chip retraining or data replay. VeRA+ preserves up to 99.77% of the drift-free accuracy after ten years of simulated drift and reduces storage overhead by more than three orders of magnitude compared with BN-based calibration. To validate VeRA+ under realistic device behavior, we extract one-week drift statistics from measurements on our fabricated 1T1R RRAM devices and use them to simulate realistic drifted weights. Under these measured drift conditions, VeRA+ achieves accuracy close to the drift-free baseline, providing an efficient and practical solution for long-term drift resilience in RRAM-IMC.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804309.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804309.summary_zh: 提出轻量漂移补偿框架VeRA+，复用共享投影矩阵并为每个漂移等级仅引入两个紧凑向量，配合离线训练与漂移感知调度，无需片上重训练。报告模拟十年漂移后保留最高99.77%无漂移精度，存储开销较BN校准降低三个数量级以上，并用 fabricated 1T1R RRAM 一周漂移测量验证。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804309.title: VeRA+: Vector-Based Lightweight Compensation for Drift-Resilient RRAM In-Memory Computing

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804310.abstract: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is promising for on-device deployment on mobile SoCs, but its multi-stage and dynamic workflow is difficult to schedule efficiently across heterogeneous processors due to accelerator affinity, shape sensitivity, and shared-memory bandwidth contention. We present HeRo, a heterogeneous-aware framework for low-latency on-device agentic RAG. It combines profiling-based performance modeling with a lightweight online scheduler to enable shape-aware partitioning, criticality-aware mapping, and bandwidth-aware concurrency control. Experiments on commercial mobile devices show up to 10.94× lower end-to-end latency over existing strategies, making practical on-device agentic RAG possible.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804310.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804310.summary_zh: 提出面向移动SoC上设备端agentic RAG的异构感知调度框架HeRo，结合性能建模与在线调度实现形状感知划分和带宽感知并发控制。报告在商用移动设备上端到端延迟最多降低10.94倍。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804310.title: HeRo: Adaptive Orchestration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Heterogeneous Mobile SoC

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804311.abstract: Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) are widely deployed in security-critical systems, making defects in their designs and synthesis toolchains potential sources of severe vulnerabilities. Existing approaches can detect miscompilations or design inconsistencies but cannot determine whether such defects are practically exploitable in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose DefVul-Risk, an automated framework that leverages a fine-tuned large language model to assess the security risk of FPGA-related defects. We construct a manually curated dataset of real-world defects and their contextual information, enabling the model to learn how to locate defects, infer their security impact, and assign risk levels with natural-language explanations. In a three-month evaluation, DefVul-Risk identified 26 previously unknown vulnerabilities, nine of which have already been assigned CVE identifiers, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804311.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804311.summary_zh: 提出DefVul-Risk框架，利用微调大语言模型评估FPGA逻辑综合工具缺陷的安全风险，构建真实缺陷数据集以定位缺陷、推断安全影响并分级。三个月评估发现26个此前未知漏洞，其中9个已获CVE编号。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804311.title: Are They All Safe? Practical Fault Injection Attacks on FPGA Logic Synthesis Tools

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804313.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have achieved remarkable performance through sparse expert activation, yet deployment on resource-constrained platforms faces severe memory challenges as their parameter size exceeds device capacity, necessitating CPU offloading. While existing systems optimize data movement and leverage CPU computation during MoE layers, they leave the CPU underutilized during GPU attention computation. We present Weaver, a stratified scheduling framework that exploits this idle window through score-stratified expert treatment. Our key insight reveals asymmetric expert importance: low-scoring experts tolerate input approximation while high-scoring ones remain accuracy-critical. Weaver proactively executes predicted low-score experts on CPU during attention using prior-layer inputs, initiates stratified prefetching for high-score experts, and reactively balances remaining workload across heterogeneous resources. Evaluations on three representative MoE models demonstrate 1.47–3.58× average speedup over state-of-the-art accuracy-preserving offloading systems while maintaining model quality.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804313.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804313.summary_zh: 提出面向内存受限MoE推理的分层专家调度框架Weaver，利用注意力计算期间CPU空闲窗口执行低分专家并分层预取高分专家。报告在三个MoE模型上相比先进精度保持型卸载系统获得1.47–3.58倍平均加速。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804313.title: Weaver: Stratified Expert Scheduling for Memory-Constrained MoE Inference

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804314.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require larger GPU memory size these days, necessitating efficient and extreme weight compression methods. Existing compression methods are either theoretically limited by 1 bit per weight or face severe performance degradation and inefficiency. To deploy LLMs in resource-constrained scenarios, we introduce UltraSketchLLM, compressing LLMs with data sketch. It reduces peak GPU memory footprint with a high compression rate down to 0.5 bit per weight. Combined with hardware-friendly implementation, UltraSketchLLM keeps tolerable performance degradation and extremely low latency overhead with 14.9x speedup compared to naive sketch solution.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804314.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804314.summary_zh: 提出UltraSketchLLM，用数据草图将LLM权重压缩至每权重0.5比特，并结合硬件友好算子降低GPU显存占用与延迟。报告相比朴素草图方案14.9倍加速。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804314.title: UltraSketchLLM: Sub-1-Bit LLM Compression via Sketch and Hardware-Friendly Operators

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804315.abstract: As the complexity of integrated circuit designs continues to escalate, the functional verification becomes increasingly challenging. Reference models, critical for accelerating the verification process, are themselves becoming more intricate and time-consuming to develop. Despite the promise shown by large language models (LLMs) in code programming, effectively generating complex reference models remains a significant hurdle. Therefore, we introduce ChipModeler, an LLM-aided agile reference model generation and verification platform. ChipModeler streamlines the transition from design specifications to fully functional reference models by integrating design standardization and hierarchical agile modeling. Employing a building-block generation strategy, it not only enhances the design capabilities of LLMs for reference models but also significantly boosts verification efficiency. We evaluated ChipModeler on 300 designs of varying complexity, demonstrating substantial improvements in both efficiency and quality of reference model generation. ChipModeler achieved a peak performance improvement of 58.99% compared to alternative methods, with notable enhancements in generation stability, and delivered a 9.18× increase in its capacity to produce reference model designs. Moreover, ChipModeler accelerates the reference model design and validation cycles by an average of 7.11× over traditional manual approaches. These results highlight the potential of ChipModeler to significantly advance the automation of reference model generation and validation.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804315.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804315.summary_zh: 提出ChipModeler，利用LLM结合设计标准化与分层敏捷建模，从设计规格生成参考模型以加速硬件功能验证。在300个不同复杂度设计上评估，生成效率与质量显著提升，峰值性能较对比方法提升58.99%。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804315.title: ChipModeler: LLM-Aided Reference Model Design for Agile Hardware Verification

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804316.abstract: Traditional logic synthesis heuristics have plateaued. We introduce ShortCircuit, a novel transformer-based architecture generating AND-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) directly from truth tables. Unlike prior deep learning efforts, we employ a two-phase training process combining supervised learning and an AlphaZero variant to navigate the doubly exponential state space. Evaluated on 500 8-input truth tables from real-world circuits, ShortCircuit guarantees functional correctness and outperforms the state-of-the-art tool ABC in circuit size. Furthermore, our greedy rollout mechanism achieves a 31X speedup, demonstrating significant efficiency gains.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804316.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804316.summary_zh: 提出ShortCircuit，用Transformer从真值表直接生成AIG，结合监督学习与AlphaZero变体搜索逻辑综合空间。在500个真实电路8输入真值表上保证功能正确，电路规模优于ABC，贪心rollout实现31倍加速。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804316.title: ShortCircuit: AlphaZero-Driven Generative Circuit Design

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804317.abstract: Transformer models have become the cornerstone of modern artificial intelligence for their ability to process sequential data with self-attention. Attention operations and large-scale matrix multiplications incur high latency and energy consumption. Hybrid computing-in-memory (CIM) architectures that integrate ReRAM and SRAM have shown great potential for Transformer acceleration. However, the inherent sparsity in the self-attention computation leads to redundant computation. Exploiting this sparsity often introduces significant overhead in Top-K query-key identification or causes accuracy degradation due to information loss from un-selected keys in prior CIM accelerators. In this work, we propose HP-CIM, a hybrid CIM accelerator that employs a ReRAM-based hash predictor (ReHP) to efficiently leverage attention sparsity. The ReHP utilizes the intrinsic conductance variation of ReRAM cells for low-cost hash projection and integrates a ReRAM content-addressable memory (CAM) with a K-winner-take-all (K-WTA) circuit for highly parallel, energy-efficient Top-K matching. Furthermore, an optimizable bias-filling strategy is introduced to restore model accuracy through a learnable bias that compensates for information loss during hash prediction. Experimental demonstration using multiple Transformer models with different tasks shows that HP-CIM achieves 9.05~310.04× higher energy efficiency and 2.48~16.93× speedup over state-of-the-art CIM-based Transformer accelerators.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804317.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804317.summary_zh: 提出HP-CIM混合CIM Transformer加速器，用ReRAM哈希预测器与CAM/K-WTA电路高效利用注意力稀疏性，并以可学习偏置补偿恢复精度。摘要片段未披露完整量化结果，但给出了架构与电路级设计贡献。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804317.title: HP-CIM: A Computing-in-Memory Transformer Accelerator with ReRAM-based Hash Predictor for Attention Sparsity Exploitation

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804319.abstract: Compact modeling for design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) is increasingly strained by device complexity, layout dependence, slow process bring-up, and the need to sweep large process spaces. Neural compact models achieve high accuracy but are hard to interpret and cumbersome to deploy in standard SPICE flows. To address these challenges and better bridge data-driven and physics-based modeling, we propose a physics-prior neural-to-symbolic compact modeling framework for DTCO based on an Efficient Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (EKAN). The framework learns Id(Vg, Vd, tOX, T) from experimentally calibrated oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (OS-FETs) TCAD dataset and then distills the EKAN teacher into a SPICE-ready symbolic current expression via KAN-derived 1D atoms, physics-aware feature design, and weighted sparse regression with smoothness-aware refinement. The resulting symbolic model uses only 116 parameters (vs. 6.4 × 102–2.6 × 103 for neural/KAN baselines) and achieves roughly 300× faster offline model build time than an MLP baseline, while maintaining comparable accuracy. It is fully interpretable, directly implementable in Verilog-A, and readily integrable into DTCO-oriented circuit simulation flows.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804319.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804319.summary_zh: 研究面向BEOL兼容DTCO的物理先验神经到符号紧凑建模框架，从OS-FET TCAD数据蒸馏出Verilog-A可实现的符号电流模型。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804319.title: A Physics-Prior Intelligent Compact Modeling Framework for BEOL-Compatible DTCO: EKAN-Based Distillation from Neural to Symbolic Models

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804320.abstract: Large language models encounter critical GPU memory capacity constraints during long-context inference, where KV cache memory consumption severely limits decode batch sizes. While existing research has explored offloading KV cache to DRAM, these approaches either demand frequent GPU-CPU data transfers or impose extensive CPU computation requirements, resulting in poor GPU utilization as the system waits for I/O operations or CPU processing to complete. We propose ScoutAttention, a novel KV cache offloading framework that accelerates LLM inference through collaborative GPU-CPU attention computation. To prevent CPU computation from bottlenecking the system, ScoutAttention introduces GPU-CPU collaborative block-wise sparse attention that significantly reduces CPU load. Unlike conventional parallel computing approaches, our framework features a novel layer-ahead CPU pre-computation algorithm, enabling the CPU to initiate attention computation one layer in advance, complemented by asynchronous periodic recall mechanisms to maintain minimal CPU compute load. Experimental results demonstrate that ScoutAttention maintains accuracy within 2.4% of baseline while achieving 2.1x speedup compared to existing offloading methods.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804320.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804320.summary_zh: 提出ScoutAttention，通过GPU-CPU协同分块稀疏注意力与层前预计算加速LLM推理的KV缓存卸载。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804320.title: ScoutAttention: Efficient KV Cache Offloading via Layer-Ahead CPU Pre-computation for LLM Inference

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804322.abstract: Analog In-Memory Computing using analog-grade memory devices promises significant speed and energy efficiency for neural network inference, but its wide-spread deployment is challenged by the unexpected computing outliers from device to circuit non-idealities. While recent efforts like defect-aware training and ensemble methods address static variation, and conventional error correcting codes (ECC) protects the stored weights, neither can detect or correct dynamic, runtime errors that occur during the analog computation itself. In this work, we propose METRIC, a Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) Error Correction Code for analog computing, which encodes the redundancy output together with the intended output using a crossbar, with a theoretical minimum of two redundancy columns. Recognizing that neural network layers have varying error sensitivities, we introduce a layer-wise deployment strategy that adaptively allocates protection, minimizing hardware overhead while maintaining target model accuracy. Furthermore, we present a complete hardware implementation, including encoder and syndrome decoder circuits that performs error detection and correction entirely in the analog domain with minimal latency. Based on experimentally measured device and circuit non-idealities, METRIC restores inference accuracy to near-baseline levels on typical CNN and Transformer models, increasing 57% and 31% accuracy compared with unprotected analog computing respectively. Evaluations show that METRIC can achieve >1000× improved area and energy efficiency over the conventional analog ECC systems, showing its great potential for building reliable and efficient IMC accelerators.

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804322.title: METRIC: An MDS-Analog ECC with Minimum Two-Column Redundancy for Fault-Tolerant, Layer-Aware IMC Architecture

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804323.abstract: The semantic gap between tensor-centric software models and signal-level hardware testbenches creates significant productivity bottlenecks in verifying Domain-Specific Accelerators (DSAs). Existing frameworks like Cocotb suffer from prohibitive synchronization overheads due to fine-grained interactions. To address this, we propose vTen, a data-centric framework that strictly decouples verification intent from execution mechanics. By leveraging a declarative DSL and kernel-granular batching, vTen minimizes hostsimulator interaction frequency. Evaluation on a production-scale 3D U-Net accelerator demonstrates that vTen achieves a 2× performance improvement in simulation latency and a 60.3% reduction in code complexity compared to Cocotb.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804323.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804323.summary_zh: 提出vTen，面向领域专用加速器的张量中心验证框架，用声明式DSL与核粒度批处理减少主机-仿真器交互。在生产级3D U-Net加速器上相比Cocotb仿真延迟降低2倍、代码复杂度减少60.3%。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804323.title: vTen: Tensor-Centric Verification Framework for Domain-Specific Accelerators

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804324.abstract: Metasurface-based photonic computing delivers ultra-high computing power density and enables ultrafast, low-power MVM. However, inverse design and system-level simulation remain prohibitively expensive due to large-scale Maxwell solvers. We present LightningFNO, a dual Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) framework that unifies inverse design and fast forward modeling for photonic MVM units. Within this framework, an inverse FNO generates candidate topologies, and a convolutional FNO subsequently predicts their optical responses, thereby facilitating deployment at the neural network level. LightningFNO achieved a speedup of 1,245,550 times compared to adjoint-based optimization for 4×4 designs while maintaining comparable accuracy. Furthermore, fabricated 3×3 prototypes demonstrated a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.043, and the system attained 97.69% accuracy on the MNIST dataset using metasurface-deployed kernels.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804324.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804324.summary_zh: 提出LightningFNO双FNO框架，用于超表面光子矩阵向量乘单元的逆向设计与快速前向建模。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804324.title: LightningFNO: Ultra-Fast Modeling and Inverse Design for Photonic Matrix-Vector Multiplication Computing Units

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804325.abstract: Real-time automotive workloads modeled as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) with probabilistic execution times face severe latency bottlenecks, where shared tasks couple multiple sensor-to-actuator paths. Minimizing end-to-end latency under such variability requires navigating a complex joint space of task mappings and offsets. To address this, we propose a Pareto-prompted metaheuristic with hierarchical mapping-then-offset refinement, utilizing Pareto dominance to search for non-dominated schedules. Evaluated on production navigation-on-autopilot workloads running on NVIDIA Orin-N-based vehicles, our method satisfies all constraints and significantly outperforms an industrial static baseline, reducing mean latency by up to 12% and 99th-percentile latency by up to 15%.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804325.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804325.summary_zh: 研究实时系统中概率DAG调度的分层Pareto提示优化，在NVIDIA Orin平台上降低端到端延迟。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804325.title: Hierarchical Pareto-Prompted Optimization for Probabilistic DAG Scheduling on Real-Time Systems

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804326.abstract: SystemVerilog Assertions (SVAs) are crucial for hardware verification. Recent studies leverage general-purpose LLMs to translate natural language properties to SVAs (NL2SVA), but they perform poorly due to limited data. We propose a data synthesis framework to tackle two challenges: the scarcity of high-quality real-world SVA corpora and the lack of reliable methods to determine NL-SVA semantic equivalence. For the former, large-scale open-source RTLs are used to guide LLMs to generate real-world SVAs; for the latter, bidirectional translation serves as a data selection method. With the synthesized data, we train SVACoder, a series of SVA generation models. Notably, SVACoder-14B achieves 75.8% on NL2SVA-Human and 84.0% on NL2SVA-Machine in Func.@1, matching or exceeding advanced LLMs like GPT-5 and DeepSeek-R1.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804326.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804326.summary_zh: 提出基于RTL的双向数据合成框架，缓解SVA语料稀缺与NL-SVA语义等价判定难题，并训练SVACoder系列断言生成模型。SVACoder-14B在NL2SVA-Human达75.8%、NL2SVA-Machine达84.0% Func.@1，匹配或超过GPT-5与DeepSeek-R1。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804326.title: SVACoder: Training Specialized LLMs for Hardware Assertion Generation via RTL-Grounded Bidirectional Data Synthesis

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804327.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN) accelerators have widely been investigated for efficient inference, where matrix multiplication commonly implemented by multiply-accumulate (MAC) units dominates the power consumption. Underscaling the supply voltage of MACs can effectively reduce the power dissipation of DNN accelerators yet induces timing errors that may degrade the inference accuracy. In this paper, we propose a bit-width adjustment circuit (denoted as ADA) for arbitrary MAC units under aggressive voltage underscaling, which adaptively tunes the critical path as per input data patterns. Incurring 16.1% area overhead, the proposed ADA enables a MAC array to achieve zero accuracy loss under voltage underscaling ratios of 0.71 and 0.72 in the inferences of multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and convolutional neural network (CNN), respectively. While preserving accuracy, the MAC array equipped with ADA achieves up to 50.89% power reduction compared to that without ADA under nominal voltage operation. Furthermore, we propose ADA-Plus to specifically optimize the MACs in output stationary systolic arrays, which reduces the area of ADA by 23%. Compared with state-of-the-art error resilient circuit designs for voltage underscaling, to achieve a similar accuracy, the proposed adaptive MAC achieves the highest voltage underscaling ratio, resulting in 14.26%–48.44% power savings for the MAC array.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804327.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804327.summary_zh: 提出可自适应调整关键路径的MAC单元ADA及面向输出驻留脉动阵列的ADA-Plus，用于激进电压欠缩放DNN加速器。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804327.title: Adaptive Multiply-Accumulate Unit with Scalable Critical Path for Aggressive Voltage Underscaling DNN Accelerators

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804328.abstract: Secure speculation schemes are critical for defeating speculative side-channel attacks, but often incur notable performance penalties, encouraging research into optimization strategies. One such optimization strategy, ReCon, improves performance by exploiting previous non-speculative data leakage to remove protections for already leaked data. However, we find that ReCon can leak secrets when an instruction depends on multiple sources of potentially secret data. We show how interactions between Speculative Taint Tracking (STT) and ReCon result in ReCon undermining STT's security guarantees. We address this oversight through a low-impact multi-source tracking mechanism that we call ReConnaissance. Together with a detailed microarchitecture, we show that, on average, ReConnaissance only lowers the overhead-reduction of ReCon from 23.5% to 18.3% on SPEC2017.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804328.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804328.summary_zh: 发现ReCon与STT交互导致多源秘密泄漏，提出ReConnaissance多源跟踪机制并给出详细微架构。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804328.title: ReConnaissance: Correctly Tracking Multiple Secrets using Reveal/Conceal Paradigms

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804329.abstract: Increasing demands for adaptability, privacy, and security at the edge have persistently pushed the frontiers for a new generation of machine learning (ML) algorithms with training and inference capabilities on-chip. Weightless Neural Network (WNN) is such an algorithm that is principled on lookup table based simple neuron structures. As a result, it offers architectural benefits, such as low-latency, low-complexity inference, compared to deep neural networks that depend heavily on multiply-accumulate operations. However, traditional WNNs rely on memorization-based one-shot training, which either leads to overfitting and reduced accuracy or requires tedious post-training adjustments, limiting their effectiveness for efficient on-chip training. In this work, we propose TsetlinWiSARD, a training approach for WNNs that leverages Tsetlin Automata (TAs) to enable probabilistic, feedback-driven learning. It overcomes the overfitting of WiSARD's one-shot training with iterative optimization, while maintaining simple, continuous binary feedback for efficient on-chip training. Central to our approach is a field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based training architecture that delivers state-of-the-art accuracy while significantly improving hardware efficiency. Our approach provides over 1000× faster training when compared with the traditional WiSARD implementation of WNNs. Further, we demonstrate 22% reduced resource usage, 93.3% lower latency, and 64.2% lower power consumption compared to FPGA-based training accelerators implementing other ML algorithms.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804329.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804329.summary_zh: 提出基于Tsetlin自动机的无权重神经网络片上训练方法，并实现FPGA训练架构。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804329.title: TsetlinWiSARD: On-Chip Training of Weightless Neural Networks using Tsetlin Automata on FPGAs

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804330.abstract: Group-wise quantization is an effective strategy for low-bit inference, where a shared scale is assigned to each small group of tensor values. However, existing formats such as Microscaling (MX) struggle to capture the diverse value distributions found across modern workloads and tensor structures. In this work, we introduce MXP, a Posit-inspired microscaling format that incorporates tapered precision to dynamically adjust exponent and fraction bits at the element level. We first observe that directly integrating the Posit format into the MX framework leads to inefficiencies in precision. By addressing this limitation, MXP achieves a more optimal balance between precision and dynamic range, thereby reducing quantization errors. We further develop a hardware accelerator tailored to MXP, featuring a simplified decoding unit and a fused multiply-accumulate (MAC) array architecture. Experimental results demonstrate that MXP achieves higher accuracy, while reducing area by 11% and 33%, and power consumption by 12% and 40%, compared to a conventional MXFP and Posit-based designs, respectively.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804330.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804330.summary_zh: 提出Posit启发的微缩放格式MXP，并设计配套解码单元与融合MAC阵列加速器。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804330.title: MXP: A Posit-Inspired Microscaling Format for Vision-Language Tasks

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804331.abstract: Scientific computing represents a class of computation-intensive workloads, creating a critical demand for in-memory computing(IMC) architectures. Although IMC has demonstrated strong performance in low-precision applications, extending it to FP64 or higher precision required by scientific computing poses significant challenges: analog IMC(AIMC) is intrinsically limited to 4-bit fixed-point precision, while digital IMC(DIMC) suffers from area and performance overheads caused by large-bit-width mantissa processing and complex exponent-alignment operations. In this paper, we propose an ultralarge bit-width IMC architecture supporting FP64 and can be extended to higher precision. The design incorporates two-step carry-save adders(TSCSA) to efficiently implement Booth mantissa multiplication, along with an exponent difference generator and FIFO-based adder tree to perform alignment and accumulation. In 28nm technology, we implemented UBFP-IMC with 168 MAC units. When executing FP64 scientific computations, it achieves 4.30× to 8.53× improvement in energy efficiency(EEF) compared to existing high-performance GPUs and AIMCs. On the basis of maintaining low accumulation latency with 27× reduction over prior work, our area benefit increases with the increase of mantissa bit-width, indicating that UBFP-IMC has excellent scalability. Application level evaluation has demonstrated the potential of our work in accelerating scientific computing. To best of our knowledge, our work is the first ultralarge bit-width digital floating-point in-memory computing accelerator designed for scientific computing.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804331.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804331.summary_zh: 提出支持FP64的超大位宽数字存内计算架构，采用两步进位保存加法器与指数对齐累加结构，并在28nm实现168个MAC单元。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804331.title: UBFP-IMC: Ultralarge Bit-Width Digital Floating-Point In-Memory Computing Accelerator for Scientific Computing

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804332.abstract: Analog circuit design is time-consuming and heavily dependent on the expertise of human designers. This paper presents a universal circuit design hierarchical model (UNCHARTED). It is the first machine learning-based framework that emulates transient simulation by modeling physical behaviors of individual circuit components through the graph neural network. The sizing of circuit elements is reflected through low-rank adaptation, and inverse design is achieved by the back-propagation mechanism. UNCHARTED can accelerate simulation by up to 241.9x, with high similarity (>95%) to SPICE simulation in more than 70% of tested circuits. Inverse design examples of a delay chain and an amplifier also demonstrate its powerful capabilities in automatic design optimization.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804332.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804332.summary_zh: 提出基于图神经网络的模拟电路瞬态仿真与逆向设计框架。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804332.title: UNCHARTED: A Universal Circuit Design Hierarchical Model based on Auto-Regressive Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network with Exogenous Driving Inputs

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804333.abstract: Flip-flops (FFs) are a critical component affecting system-level power, performance, and area (PPA). Many logic-based FF design methods have been introduced to expand the scope of topology exploration beyond intuition. However, their exploration scope is still limited to 2-bit finite state machines (FSMs) because of inefficient search space representation. We present B-Flex, an automated FF FSM search that integrates a complete, graph-based behavioral equivalence check into a pruning-based generative search. This efficient and scalable approach vastly expands the design space and allows exhaustive exploration of 3-bit-state FSMs. B-Flex has identified over 568 million valid FF mechanisms, including many novel 3-bit-state FF designs. Topology synthesis on 20 sampled FSMs has produced several high-performance FF circuits that outperform conventional FFs. For instance, FF1, achieves a 2.53X speedup over a transmission-gate FF (TGFF) and improved metastability window at 0.9 V.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804333.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804333.summary_zh: 提出基于FSM穷举搜索的触发器设计空间探索方法，将图行为等价检查集成到剪枝生成搜索中，扩展到3位状态FSM。报告识别超过5.68亿个有效FF机制，采样拓扑综合得到FF1较传输门FF提速2.53倍并改善0.9V下亚稳态窗口。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804333.title: B-Flex: Exploration of Broader Flip-Flop Design Space Based on FSM Exhaustive Search

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804334.abstract: Modern cloud servers routinely co-locate multiple latency-sensitive microservice instances to improve resource efficiency. However, the diversity of microservice behaviors, coupled with mutual performance interference under simultaneous multithreading (SMT), makes large-scale placement increasingly complex. Existing interference aware schedulers and isolation techniques rely on coarse core-level profiling or static resource partitioning, leaving asymmetric hyperthread-level heterogeneity and SMT contention dynamics largely unmodeled. We present Hestia, a hyperthread-level, interference-aware scheduling framework powered by self-attention. Through an extensive analysis of production traces encompassing 32,408 instances across 3,132 servers, we identify two dominant contention patterns—sharing-core (SC) and sharingsocket (SS)-and reveal strong asymmetry in their impact. Guided by these insights, Hestia incorporates (1) a self-attention-based CPU usage predictor that models SC/SS contention and hardware heterogeneity, and (2) an interference scoring model that estimates pairwise contention risks to guide scheduling decisions. We evaluate Hestia through large-scale simulation and a real production deployment. Hestia reduces the 95th-percentile service latency by up to 80%, lowers overall CPU consumption by 2.3% under the same workload, and surpasses five state-of-the-art schedulers by up to 30.65% across diverse contention scenarios.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804334.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804334.summary_zh: 研究云微服务的超线程级干扰感知调度框架。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804334.title: Hestia: Hyperthread-Level Scheduling for Cloud Microservices with Interference-Aware Attention

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804335.abstract: Weight-only quantized large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a standard paradigm for memory-efficient deployment, motivating mixed-precision (FP-INT) arithmetic between integer (INT) quantized weights (Qweights) and floating-point (FP) activations. While FP-INT GEMM accelerators facilitate their execution, prior designs incur high accumulation overheads, underutilize the parallelism of low-precision Qweights, and lack versatility. To address this, we propose CAPA, a convertibility-aware accelerator optimized for asymmetric GEMM, where operands exhibit significant bit-wise precision differences. We introduce Hybrid Delta Block Floating Point (HDBFP), a novel format that converts FP activations to INT while preserving accuracy, thereby maximizing the efficiency of INT-based processing elements (PEs). In addition, our data decomposition scheme significantly enhances computation parallelism for low-precision Qweights within a unified hardware datapath. Together, the CAPA architecture ensures full versatility across common FP16/BF16-INT8/INT4 combinations. Extensive evaluations show that CAPA maintains high accuracy comparable to a GPU baseline across language evaluation benchmarks, improving area efficiency by 3.98× and power efficiency by 4.38× over the FP-FP baseline.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804335.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804335.summary_zh: 提出面向权重量化LLM非对称GEMM的混合精度加速器CAPA，引入HDBFP格式将FP激活转为INT并设计统一数据通路的数据分解方案。摘要片段称其覆盖FP16/BF16-INT8/INT4组合并保持与GPU基线相当的精度，但截断片段未披露完整性能数据。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804335.title: CAPA: Convertibility-Aware Mixed-Precision Accelerator for Asymmetric GEMM in Weight-Only Quantized LLMs

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804336.abstract: As conventional FinFET architectures encounter severe scaling limitations, Complementary-FET (CFET) technology with vertically stacked PMOS and NMOS transistors has emerged as a promising solution for continued standard cell density scaling. However, aggressive area compaction in CFET standard cells drastically limits intra-cell routing resources, leading to routing congestion and design rule challenges. To mitigate this issue, multi-row CFET standard cell architectures have been introduced to improve intra-cell routability and alleviate blocklevel congestion. Nevertheless, these multi-row configurations introduce new placement-routing coupling and design rule complexities, making it challenging to achieve compact, DRC-clean, and routable layouts. Therefore, this work proposes an area-optimal and routability-driven layout synthesis framework for multi-row CFET cells, which effectively addresses the challenges of area efficiency, constrained pin accessibility, and DRC compliance under multi-row CFET architectures. The framework integrates three key methodologies: (1) an Euler-guided transistor partitioning with multi-strategy graph-theoretic pruning to achieve optimal area; (2) an Euler-path-based placement with a combined metric of wirelength and access pin count to improve routability; and (3) a two-stage Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT)-based routing flow consisting of a Multi-Commodity Flow (MCF)-based routability-guaranteed pin-access selection and an Integer Linear Programming (ILP)-enhanced hierarchical routing to ensure DRC/LVS closure. Compared with state-of-the-art multi-row CFET cell generators, experimental results show that our algorithm consistently achieves the optimal layout area, while delivering significant improvements in solution quality and efficiency.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804336.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804336.summary_zh: 提出面向多行CFET标准单元的面积最优且可布线性驱动的版图综合框架，集成Euler引导晶体管划分与图论剪枝等方法。摘要片段未披露具体面积或DRC结果数据。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804336.title: Area-Optimal and Routability-Driven Layout Synthesis for Multi-Row Complementary-FET Standard Cells

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804337.abstract: Emerging tree-structured speculative decoding has been proposed as a promising alternative to conventional sequence-structured speculative decoding, offering a higher verification success rate and reduced inference latency while exhibiting characteristics of higher computational intensity. However, existing near-memory processing (NMP)-enabled heterogeneous accelerators for large language models (LLMs) typically place processing elements (PEs) on DRAM dies, resulting in limited computation capability, which prevents them from fully accelerating tree-structured speculative decoding. In response, we propose a hybrid-bonding (HB)-based heterogeneous accelerator for tree-structured speculative decoding, called HBSpec, which customizes PEs on the incorporated logic die to enhance NMP computation capacity. HBSpec features a communication-optimized data mapping policy to minimize cross-bank data access overhead inherent in the distributed-memory design adopted in HB. Furthermore, an arithmetic intensity-aware operator scheduler is designed to dynamically assign operators to the most suitable hardware units, while a Tree-KV pool management scheme is introduced to eliminate memory fragmentation caused by discarded speculative branches. Experimental results demonstrate that HBSpec achieves average throughput improvements of 15.56×, 2.36×, and 2.13× over the state-of-the-art NPU-only, NPU+LPDDR, and NPU+HB baselines, respectively.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804337.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804337.summary_zh: 提出基于混合键合的异构加速器HBSpec，将PE置于逻辑die以加速树结构推测解码，并设计通信优化数据映射与算子调度。摘要片段未披露完整性能结果。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804337.title: HBSpec: A Hybrid-Bonding-based Heterogeneous Accelerator for Efficient Tree-Structured Speculative Decoding

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804338.abstract: Technology scaling in embedded Mixed-Criticality (MC) systems intensifies reliability challenges, impacting both reliable execution of MC applications and underlying hardware. Ensuring real-time and safety requirements is essential in these MC systems. While some studies have explored applying fault tolerance techniques in MC systems in multiple abstraction layers separately, such isolated layer-specific fault mitigation incurs high overheads in peak power, resources, energy, and timing, making it impractical for most embedded MC systems. In this regard, we propose a novel scheme to address cross-layer reliability in MC systems at design-time, by providing application-specific, low-cost fault tolerance. This approach distributes fault mitigation across multiple layers to minimize it on the hardware layer, ultimately resulting in more cost-effective system designs. To achieve this, we introduce a machine-learning-based approach to select efficient fault-tolerance methods across multiple layers, reducing overheads while meeting the real-time and reliability requirements. Experimental results demonstrate our scheme meets reliability constraints for all task criticality levels, outperforming single-layer method, while reducing peak power and energy consumption by an average of 27.55% and 48.32%, respectively. Compared to state-of-the-art, it achieves 50.54% lower peak power and 76.67% lower energy, while meeting the requirements.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804338.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804338.summary_zh: 研究嵌入式混合关键系统中的跨层可靠性管理与容错方法选择。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804338.title: XRel-Graph: Graph Learning-Driven Cross-Layer Reliability Management in Embedded Mixed-Criticality Systems

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804339.abstract: In resource-constrained tiny edge devices like MCUs, deploying data/compute-intensive AI like CNNs is challenging. Compute-in-Memory (CIM) and Binary Neural Networks (BNN) offer promising solutions by reducing memory access and simplifying computational load. We propose COM-BNN, a configurable low-power accelerator integrating MRAM-based CIM with serial BNN computation. It introduces a temporal configurable input mechanism and an Integrate-and-Fire (IF) adder for serial MAC operations, plus an Exact Result Inferring (ERI) method for efficient binary convolutional computations. COM-BNN achieves up to 85% energy and 83% power reduction over ADC-based CIM baselines, and enables dynamic latency-power tradeoffs, dropping power to 0.03% in serial mode for edge adaptability.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804339.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804339.summary_zh: 提出MRAM存内计算的可配置低功耗二值卷积加速器COM-BNN，采用串行BNN计算、可配置输入机制与Integrate-and-Fire加法器。报告较ADC型CIM基线降低最高85%能耗和83%功耗，串行模式功耗可降至0.03%。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804339.title: COM-BNN: A Configurable Low Power MRAM-based Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for Binary Convolutional Computations

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804340.abstract: Recent studies show that incorporating Processing-in-Memory (PIM) into neural processing units (NPUs) can significantly improve the efficiency of large language model (LLM) inference on edge devices. However, the limited compute capability of DRAM-PIM and the use of fixed dataflow strategies still constrain overall performance gains. To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid PIM architecture that integrates non-volatile spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory (SOT-MRAM)-based PIM into existing NPU-PIM systems, fully exploiting the high compute capability and bandwidth of SOT-MRAM together with the large storage capacity of DRAM. On top of this architecture, we further design an adaptive compute scheduling and dataflow optimization framework. Using NSGA-II-based multi-objective dataflow space exploration, our framework identifies Pareto-optimal hardware resource allocations and dataflow configurations under different deployment objectives. Experimental results show that our approach reduces inference latency by up to 8.72× and energy consumption by 11.74× compared to NPUs, and further achieves 6.24× lower latency and 7.76× higher energy efficiency than NPU-PIM baselines.
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804340.journal: Proceedings of the 63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804340.summary_zh: 提出融合SOT-MRAM PIM与NPU-PIM的异构LLM推理架构，并用NSGA-II进行数据流空间探索。报告较NPU降低最高8.72倍延迟和11.74倍能耗，较NPU-PIM基线延迟低6.24倍、能效高7.76倍。
doi:10.1145/3770743.3804340.title: Hybrid PIM-oriented Architecture-Dataflow Co-Design for Heterogeneous LLM Inference

doi:10.1145/3770743.3804341.abstract: Verification flows use Verification IPs (VIPs) to identify assertion violations. This is well-suited for on-chip protocols (e.g., AXI, AHB) with standard specifications (e.g., AMBA) for developers to write assertions that detect violations. Patching these violations, however, still requires manual effort. A good patch must not only fix the violation but also preserve functionality (e.g., pass the testsuite) without causing new violations. We propose Stitch, based on the intuition that given an implementation, a violated assertion, and a counterexample an LLM can try to synthesize patches. To evaluate Stitch, we develop a new dataset that comprises 100 violations in 11 implementations of 5 protocols (AXI, AHB, APB, Wishbone, and TileLink). Our first experiment reports 19% success rate across 4 LLMs (GPT4, GPT5, Gemini, and Claude).
