doi:10.1145/3843236.title: PrefixAgent: An LLM-Powered Design Framework for Efficient Prefix Adder Optimization

doi:10.1145/3844511.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong performance across applications, but their inference is computationally intensive, posing significant challenges for edge deployment. Quantization is among the most effective and widely used optimizations. In particular, ternary-weight quantization further lowers compute cost by replacing many multiplications with lightweight additions, thereby reducing complexity and energy. However, existing GPU/ASIC solutions often exhibit low utilization for ternary-weight LLMs and fail to exploit their inherent sparsity, leading to inefficient execution. To address this, we propose SATLLM, a lightweight accelerator optimized for ternary weights and sparsity. At the algorithm level, we propose a co-optimization method based on unstructured pruning and ternary-weight clustering to effectively enhance the sparsity. To further exploit this sparsity, we design a hardware-friendly sparsity-aware merging scheme and develop a customized BitLinear engine to support efficient sparse computation. In addition, we optimize the dataflow between the BitLinear engine and the GEMM unit, effectively alleviating performance bottlenecks caused by workload imbalance. Together, these optimizations significantly improve the throughput and energy efficiency of ternary-weight LLM inference. The experiments show that our proposed accelerator achieves an energy efficiency of 9.42 TOPS/W, with improvements of up to 42.41 ×, 16.99 ×, 4.42 ×, 2.49 ×, and 1.90 × compared to NVIDIA V100, A100, ANT, MECLA, and RMFA, respectively.
doi:10.1145/3844511.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3844511.summary_zh: 提出面向三值权重LLM的稀疏感知加速器SATLLM，算法层用非结构化剪枝与三值权重聚类提升稀疏度，硬件层设计稀疏感知合并方案与定制BitLinear引擎。并优化BitLinear引擎与GEMM单元间的数据流以缓解负载不均衡瓶颈。
doi:10.1145/3844511.title: SATLLM: A Sparsity-aware Accelerator for Ternary-Weight Large Language Models

doi:10.1145/3846380.abstract: The existing computer-aided design approaches for Digital Microfluidic Biochips focus on optimising execution time and electrode utilisation, but overlook security verification overhead as a synthesis constraint. The advanced detection method, based on ResNet-50 deep neural networks with 98% accuracy, requires three to four orders of magnitude more computational capacity (3.8 GFLOPS) than the embedded biochip controllers. Existing reactive recovery approaches suffer from prohibitive latency, with re-synthesis algorithms requiring seconds to 33 minutes on desktop processors, causing timing violations incompatible with real-time bioassay constraints. We present a security-aware computer-aided design framework, called FASP (Fault-Aware Synthesis and Partitioning), that integrates the computational cost of verification as a design-time synthesis constraint through hardware and software partitioning to enable effective placement of the detection method. The formulation of a multi-objective optimisation problem for security integration across diverse computing substrates is presented, along with a synthesis algorithm with O ( k · r · n log n ) complexity. The algorithm performs critical path analysis, selective module replication, and communication fabric synthesis to adapt the verification pipeline configuration to meet real-time deadlines and reliability requirements before deployment. Experimental results show this method yields an average verification success rate of 84.44% (over 5.59% better than the nearest baseline placements) across system scales from 4 to 324. The proposed method achieves synthesis times of 16–50 ms on average for redundancy levels 3–6, while an overall average latency of 128.86 ms enables the integration of verification directly into the design-time phase.
doi:10.1145/3846380.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3846380.summary_zh: 面向数字微流控生物芯片，将安全验证计算开销作为综合约束，提出故障感知的软硬件划分框架与多目标优化算法。
doi:10.1145/3846380.title: FASP: A Fault-Aware Hardware/Software Partitioning Framework for Security Verification in Reliable Digital Microfluidic Biochips

doi:10.1145/3846381.abstract: FPGAs are increasingly used in cloud computing infrastructures and reconfigurable system-on-chip, particularly for AI acceleration. The availability of FPGAs in cloud data centers has opened up new opportunities for users to improve application performance by implementing customizable hardware accelerators directly on the FPGA fabric. To improve resource utilization and flexibility, FPGAs allow multi-tenancy, in which multiple users share a single FPGA through dynamic partial reconfiguration. However, the virtualization and sharing of FPGA resources among multiple users open up new security vulnerabilities during reconfiguration. For instance, an adversary can inject faults into partial bitstreams during the reconfiguration process. Unlike prior runtime fault attacks, the injected faults become embedded in the bitstream and persist after configuration, continuing to corrupt FPGA operation even after the attack ceases. Cyclic redundancy check (CRC) is used in commercial FPGA toolchains for bitstream integrity verification, but CRC is insufficient against reconfiguration-time fault attacks. In particular, CRC performs coarse-grained, post-load bitstream verification, which prevents early detection of bitstream manipulation and can induce denial-of-service by forcing the configuration interface into an error state that blocks subsequent benign bitstreams. To address these limitations, we present a lightweight countermeasure that integrates ASCON, a standardized cryptographic authentication primitive, directly into the reconfiguration flow to detect and block fault-injected bitstreams from configuration. Experimental results on a Xilinx Pynq FPGA platform demonstrate preemptive detection and fine-grained localization of fault-injected regions within the bitstream, while incurring low overhead.
doi:10.1145/3846381.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3846381.summary_zh: 针对多租户FPGA重配置期故障注入攻击，指出商用CRC仅做粗粒度加载后校验不足以防护，并提出基于ASCON的防御机制。论文关注注入故障持久驻留于部分比特流并持续破坏FPGA运行的问题。
doi:10.1145/3846381.title: Faults that Persist: Fault-Injection Attacks and ASCON-Based Defense in Multi-Tenant FPGAs

doi:10.1145/3847663.abstract: Side-channel attacks (SCAs) pose critical security threats to neural networks (NNs) deployed on hardware platforms, particularly in cloud-based Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) environments. This paper introduces a channel-level parallel structure for matrix operations to enhance NN resilience against SCAs, which mainly targets convolutional layers in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and multi-head attention layers in Transformers. Unlike kernel-level parallelism which is the common base of parallel structure for FPGA NN Accelerator, our methodology reorganizes computational sequences by associating single inputs with weights from multiple CNN channels or multiple Query/Key/Value (Q/K/V) matrices across Transformer heads. This strategy effectively thwarts Correlation Power Analysis (CPA) attacks targeting layer weight extraction. Comprehensive evaluation on PYNQ-Z2 FPGA demonstrates significant security improvements over state-of-the-art masking techniques. For CNN convolutional layers, SCA success rates drop from \(96.98\% \) to \(7.27\% \) on average. The architecture achieves either: low resource overhead ( \(87.3\% \) average reduction vs. state-of-the-art masking method) or enhanced timing performance ( \(51.37\% \) average improvement vs. baseline). Similarly, Transformer multi-head attention layers exhibit reduced SCA success rates from \(86.98\% \) to \(7.03\% \) on average, with either \(73.35\% \) resource reduction on average or \(31.94\% \) timing improvement on average. Additional analysis examines weight distribution impact across channels for precise security assessment. Results confirm the proposed structure provides robust SCA protection for secure NN hardware deployment.
doi:10.1145/3847663.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3847663.summary_zh: 针对FPGA上神经网络加速器的侧信道攻击，提出通道级并行矩阵运算结构，将单输入与多通道权重或多个Q/K/V矩阵关联以打乱计算序列。在PYNQ-Z2上评估，CNN卷积层CPA攻击成功率平均从96.98%降至7.27%，并报告资源开销较掩码方法平均降低87.3%。
doi:10.1145/3847663.title: Defending Side-Channel Attacks in FPGA-based Convolutional Layers and Multi-Head Attention Layers with Channel-Level Parallelization

doi:10.1145/3847673.abstract: Design and technology co-optimization (DTCO) is the process of optimizing technology and design concurrently to enhance the performance, power, and area (PPA) of semiconductors, in which an essential ingredient is to evaluate technologies, design rules, and cell architectures using block-level PPA analysis. In this paper, we propose a novel DTCO framework assisted by machine learning (ML) for advanced process nodes. The key features of our framework are: (1) precise analysis of DTCO parameter changes in real time as well as identification of optimal DTCO parameter configurations within an acceptable runtime; (2) a full exploration of PPA metrics through standard cell (SC) library generation and PPA evaluation, for which we develop a new algorithm that accelerates the necessary physical design process; (3) supporting both Complementary-FET (CFET)-based SCs and multi-row-height SCs. Through experiments with benchmark circuits, we show that our DTCO framework preserves trends in PPA changes and precisely identifies optimal DTCO parameter sets while substantially improving efficiency. In addition, it is shown that our SC layout generator supporting CFET-based SCs and multi-row-height SCs provides a timely DTCO process relevant to ongoing technology advancements.
doi:10.1145/3847673.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3847673.summary_zh: 提出机器学习辅助的DTCO框架，通过标准单元库生成与PPA评估实时分析DTCO参数并搜索最优配置，并开发加速物理设计流程的算法。框架支持CFET与多行高单元，实验表明其保持PPA变化趋势并显著提升效率。
doi:10.1145/3847673.title: ML-assisted Design Technology Co-Optimization Framework for Advanced Process Nodes: Analysis and Exploration of DTCO Parameters using PPA of Digital Blocks

doi:10.1145/3848639.abstract: Analog routing must balance design rules and layout constraints while managing interconnect resistance and capacitance. Many analog-routing frameworks combine wirelength objectives with constraint handling and evaluate detailed parasitic effects after routing. This separation motivates investigating whether low-latency parasitic estimates can guide candidate expansions during routing. We present APEC-Route, an analog-routing framework that combines interval-tree-based wire segmentation, a multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based neighbor-aware total-capacitance model, and analytical wire-resistance evaluation. The resulting estimates guide the search in parasitic-minimization and parasitic-matching modes. On four finalized 65 nm layouts, the extractor attains a geometric-mean relative error of 5.54–6.77% and a mean absolute percentage error of 7.41–9.93% against the field-solver reference; each in-search query takes 251–345 μ s. For each of three 65 nm block-level routed-circuit cases—an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA), a comparator, and a capacitive digital-to-analog converter (CDAC)—SAGERoute and the w/o-R/C, R-only, CC-only, and full APEC-Route variants use the same fixed placement. Across both controlled capacitance-term comparisons, enabling the capacitance term improves eight of nine independent circuit metrics, with OTA phase margin as the sole exception. The derived ENOB increases consistently with SINAD. Relative to w/o R/C, the full objective increases OTA gain and CMRR by 2.7 and 1.0 dB and UGB by 0.01 MHz, reduces comparator delay, hysteresis voltage, and offset voltage by 20.5%, 16.0%, and 26.6%, and reduces CDAC delay by 10.4% while increasing SINAD by 16.4 dB; OTA phase margin decreases by 1.1°.
doi:10.1145/3848639.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3848639.summary_zh: 提出模拟布线框架APEC-Route，结合区间树线网分段、MLP邻居感知总电容模型与解析电阻评估，在65 nm版图上提取误差几何平均5.54–6.77%。
doi:10.1145/3848639.title: APEC-Route: Guiding Analog Routing with On-the-Fly Parasitic Extraction Based on a Neural Capacitance Model

doi:10.1145/3849810.abstract: Transmission delays are inherent in silicon photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and have a significant impact on their dynamic behavior and system-level performance. However, conventional modeling and simulation approaches often overlook or inadequately account for these delays, limiting accuracy and efficiency in circuit-level analysis. This paper presents a delay-aware macromodeling methodology that explicitly extracts time delays from frequency-domain responses and incorporates them into a compact pole-residue representation. In contrast to traditional techniques such as complex vector fitting (CVF), which approximate delay effects indirectly and often require a large number of poles, resulting in increased model complexity, reduced simulation efficiency, and potential causality violations, the proposed method captures delays explicitly and compactly without compromising accuracy or physical consistency. To enable integration into circuit simulation workflows, we introduce an efficient Verilog-A implementation of the proposed model, along with practical strategies for representing time delays within standard electronic-photonic co-simulation environments. The proposed approach is validated using three categories of passive PIC structures: waveguides, feedforward multi-path circuits, and resonant (loop-based) circuits, demonstrating superior compactness, simulation speed, and accuracy compared to conventional modeling techniques. These results highlight the method’s potential for scalable and high-fidelity modeling of PICs in hybrid electronic-photonic circuit and system design.
doi:10.1145/3849810.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3849810.summary_zh: 研究硅光子集成电路的延迟感知Verilog-A宏建模与仿真框架。
doi:10.1145/3849810.title: A Delay-Aware Verilog-A Modeling and Simulation Framework for Passive Photonic Integrated Circuits

doi:10.1145/3849812.abstract: The increasing scale of System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures exacerbates the reliability risks of single-particle radiation effects, rendering traditional exhaustive gate-level fault injection prohibitively slow. To address this, we propose SSRESF-OPT, an end-to-end simulation and optimization framework combining accelerated dynamic fault injection with machine learning-driven prediction. The framework first introduces a cross-layer static binding mechanism to eliminate runtime string resolution, reducing per-injection simulation overhead to \(\mathcal {O}(1) \) complexity. Building on this optimized engine, an SVM-based classification pipeline, guided by structural clustering, accurately predicts the radiation vulnerability of unsimulated circuit nodes using netlist-derived features. To maximize resource efficiency, an OPT-based top- k hardening strategy is then employed to prioritize critical architectural bottlenecks. Evaluations across 15 gate-level netlists, including massive AES subsystems and RISC-V PULP SoCs, demonstrate the framework’s efficacy. The model-assisted approach achieves an average end-to-end runtime speedup of 6.35 × over the highly optimized simulation baseline while maintaining a 94.58% prediction accuracy. Furthermore, hardening only the top 10% of ranked nodes reduces system Soft Error Rate (SER) by 85%, providing a fast and actionable methodology for radiation-hardened microprocessor design.
doi:10.1145/3849812.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3849812.summary_zh: 该文提出SSRESF-OPT框架，用于SoC单粒子辐射效应仿真与加固优化，通过跨层静态绑定将单次注入仿真开销降至O(1)，并用SVM结合结构聚类预测未仿真节点的辐射脆弱性，再以OPT进行top-k加固。在包括AES子系统和RISC-V PULP SoC的15个门级网表上，模型辅助方法相比高度优化仿真基线平均端到端加速6.35倍。
doi:10.1145/3849812.title: SSRESF-OPT: A Sensitivity-Aware Framework for Single-Particle Radiation Effects Simulation and Optimization in SoC Platforms Using Machine Learning

doi:10.1145/3849869.abstract: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) design productivity is often constrained by manual, expert-driven pragma tuning and the difficulty of balancing performance optimization with strict hardware resource limits. While automated Design Space Exploration (DSE) has been extensively studied, many existing approaches rely on open-loop estimation models or substantial training data, which can lead to physically unrealizable designs under tight resource budgets. In this work, we propose Reflex-HLS , a training-free agentic framework that formulates HLS optimization as a closed-loop, feedback-driven process grounded in physical synthesis outcomes. Reflex-HLS integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) within a Planner–Actor–Critic architecture, where optimization decisions are iteratively refined based on hardware-in-the-loop feedback from the vendor toolchain, ensuring physical realizability throughout the optimization process. Experimental results on PolyBench and MachSuite benchmarks, validated through full Vivado synthesis and implementation, demonstrate that Reflex-HLS achieves speedups of up to 48.41 × (e.g., on jacobi-2d ) while strictly adhering to device resource constraints. Further evaluations across regular, irregular, and structured workloads show that the proposed framework generalizes beyond conventional compute kernels. Comparative studies against representative open-loop DSE methods, large foundation models operating without hardware feedback, and closed-loop heuristic search highlight the trade-offs among optimization paradigms, with Reflex-HLS producing more deployable and resource-efficient designs under tight resource budgets in the evaluated cases.
doi:10.1145/3849869.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3849869.summary_zh: 提出Reflex-HLS，一种免训练的多角色LLM智能体框架，以Planner–Actor–Critic闭环结合Vivado综合实现反馈迭代优化HLS pragma。在PolyBench与MachSuite上经完整综合实现验证，报告最高48.41倍加速并满足器件资源约束。
doi:10.1145/3849869.title: Constraint-aware HLS optimization via LLM-based multi-role agent with iterative reflexion

doi:10.1145/3856825.abstract: Recently, the use of large language models (LLMs) for Verilog code generation has attracted great research interest to enable hardware design automation. However, previous works have shown a gap between the ability of LLMs and the practical demands of hardware description language (HDL) engineering. This gap includes differences in how engineers phrase questions and hallucinations in the generated code. To address these challenges, we introduce HaVen , a novel LLM framework designed to mitigate hallucinations and align Verilog code generation with the practices of HDL engineers. HaVen tackles hallucination issues by proposing a comprehensive taxonomy and employing a chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism to translate symbolic modalities ( e .g. truth tables, state diagrams, e tc.) into accurate natural language descriptions. Furthermore, HaVen bridges this gap by using a data augmentation strategy, synthesizing high-quality instruction-code pairs that match real HDL engineering practices. Building upon HaVen , we develop HaVen -R, a reasoning-augmented extension fine-tuned with a Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RFT) Dataset and a Reasoning Dataset, enabling Chain-of-Thought (CoT) guided self-reflection to iteratively repair Verilog code. We further introduce HaVen -Agent, a multi-agent system that orchestrates a Planner Agent (GPT-4o), a Coder Agent ( HaVen -R), and a Verifier Agent for iterative code repair. Our experiments demonstrate that HaVen -Agent significantly improves the correctness of Verilog code generation, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on VerilogEval and RTLLM benchmarks. Additional evaluations include a 400-case multi-generator repair study, component and iteration ablations, CVDP, end-to-end cost and latency analysis, and protocol-aware comparisons with recent feedback, agentic, and reasoning-augmented methods. HaVen is publicly available at https://github.com/Intelligent-Computing-Research-Group/HaVen.
doi:10.1145/3856825.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3856825.summary_zh: 提出 HaVen 多智能体 LLM 框架，通过幻觉分类、思维链将真值表/状态图转为自然语言，并用数据增强生成贴近 HDL 工程实践的指令-代码对，以改进 Verilog 代码生成与修复。给定摘要片段未披露完整实验与量化结果。
doi:10.1145/3856825.title: HaVen-Agent: Enhancing Hallucination-Mitigated Verilog Code Generation Aligned with HDL Engineers through Code Repair and Multi-Agent Orchestration

doi:10.1145/3857917.abstract: Hybrid-row-height IC design incorporates placement rows of two or more distinct heights which do not have to be integer multiples of a single height. This design strategy is more flexible for optimizing power, performance, and area simultaneously. Several attempts have been made to deal with the hybrid-row-height standard cell placement problem with customizable row configuration by intelligently leveraging a commercial placement tool. Here we propose an enhanced algorithm, Best Match, to determine the best matching row configuration for a given netlist which leads to minimal disturbance to the initial timing-optimized placement after placement legalization. Our row planning approach has a number of enhancements over previous works, including (1) consideration of horizontal displacement of cells in addition to vertical displacement of cells, (2) precise positioning of the hybrid rows, and (3) ability to handle macros in a design. As a result, we obtained a much smaller total displacement of cells after placement legalization compared to the state-of-the-art works. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms the flow-based method in [9] with 48.4%, 24.9%, and 68.8% reduction in the total displacement of cells, final routed wirelength, and post-route total negative slack, respectively. It yielded 13.4% reduction in the total displacement of cells, 4.5% reduction in the final routed wirelength, and 26.3% reduction in the post-route total negative slack compared to [7]. Furthermore, compared to the legalized placement generated by a commercial tool under the uniformly hybrid row configuration, the routed wirelength and post-route total negative slack are reduced by 27.4% and 91.8%, respectively, under the customized row configuration determined by Best Match.
doi:10.1145/3857917.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3857917.summary_zh: 针对混合行高标准单元布局，提出Best Match算法为网表确定最佳行配置，在合法化后最小化对时序优化初始布局的扰动，并考虑单元水平位移、混合行精确定位及宏单元阻塞处理。实验显示相对文献[9]的流程式方法在位移指标上分别改善48.4%、24.9%和68.8%。
doi:10.1145/3857917.title: Best Match: Enhanced Hybrid-Row-Height Standard Cell Placement with Macro Blockages

doi:10.1145/3858342.abstract: Graph accelerators have emerged as a promising solution for accelerating the processing of large-scale sparse graphs by leveraging the in-situ computation capabilities of ReRAM crossbars. However, existing designs incur substantial memristor access overhead due to the large number of graph partitions, increasing execution time and energy consumption while reducing circuit lifetime. This paper presents REUSE, a ReRAM-based graph accelerator that exploits recurring subgraph patterns to minimize memristor write operations. REUSE identifies frequent patterns and maps them to static graph engines whose crossbar configurations are preserved throughout execution, while less frequent patterns are assigned to dynamic engines at runtime. To support efficient mapping, REUSE employs a lightweight host-side processing scheme that operates directly on the graph's coordinate list, avoiding costly dense matrix reconstruction. Patterns are then distributed across multiple crossbars within each graph engine to balance the workload and maximize utilization. Furthermore, we develop analytical execution-time and energy models and use them to explore key architectural parameters, including the allocation of static and dynamic graph engines. REUSE is evaluated on diverse real-world graph datasets using BFS, SSSP, and PageRank, with BFS as the common workload for comparison against four state-of-the-art ReRAM-based accelerators. It achieves average speedups of 6.9 × over SparseMEM, 4.2 × over RPBFS, and 2.5 × over TARe, and improves on GraphR by 76 ×. The corresponding energy-delay product reductions are 7.5 ×, 70 ×, and 4.9 × against the same three designs, and approximately five orders of magnitude against GraphR. Circuit lifetime is extended by 2 × over SparseMEM and by two orders of magnitude over GraphR.
doi:10.1145/3858342.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3858342.summary_zh: REUSE是一种基于ReRAM的图处理加速器，利用重复出现的子图模式减少忆阻器写操作，将高频模式映射到配置保持不变的静态图引擎，低频模式运行时分配给动态引擎，并采用轻量级主机端坐标列表处理与跨crossbar负载均衡。论文还建立了执行时间与能耗分析模型用于探索关键架构参数；给定摘要片段未披露具体加速比或能耗数值。
doi:10.1145/3858342.title: REUSE: Recurrent Subgraph Exploitation for ReRAM-Accelerated Graph Processing

doi:10.1145/3859871.abstract: Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based emulation delivers orders of magnitude higher throughput than software simulation. However, fundamental clocking differences between application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and FPGAs limit its performance and capacity. To address this, we model the sampling of all flip-flops (FFs), originally triggered by multiple generated clocks, as an ordered sequence of events and reproduce their behavior at each emulation step. We introduce two clock models. The output-gated model (M o ) samples the clock, input, and output of each FF, requiring more logic resources but no event ordering. Conversely, the sampling-gated model (M s ) uses clock edge detection to conditionally sample, using fewer logic resources but requiring event ordering. We then adopt a hybrid strategy that applies M o to clock-generation logic to avoid resolving complex clock dependencies, and applies M s to the data path to save logic resources. We formally prove that the transformed design is sequentially equivalent to the original at every emulation step. We propose matching-point inductive verification (MPIV), which augments the inductive proof with matching points recorded during the transformation and reduces verification tasks to satisfiability (SAT) checks. Across industrial designs with up to 11,515 generated clocks, the hybrid approach incurs modest overhead (1.7% FFs and 5.8% lookup tables (LUTs) on average). MPIV achieves up to 2,950 × speedup and succeeds on large designs where a widely used model checker ABC-PDR times out. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first publicly documented and formally verified methodology for eliminating logic-generated clocks in ASIC-to-FPGA emulation.
doi:10.1145/3859871.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3859871.summary_zh: 针对FPGA仿真中ASIC多生成时钟的采样建模，提出输出门控与采样门控两种时钟模型及混合策略，并形式化证明变换后设计每步顺序等价。进一步提出匹配点归纳验证MPIV。
doi:10.1145/3859871.title: Provably Correct and Scalable Clock Modeling for FPGA-based Emulation

doi:10.1145/3859873.abstract: In recent years, a novel non-invasive laser-assisted attack known as Optical Probing (OP) has been demonstrated to effectively probe the internal state of integrated circuits. This attack exploits the relative transparency of the silicon substrate to Near-InfraRed (NIR) light, enabling optical access through the backside of the chip. Consequently, OP poses a significant threat to information processed or stored on the chip and may facilitate Intellectual Property (IP) theft or reverse engineering. Existing mitigation techniques can be broadly classified into three categories: (1) fabrication-level modifications, (2) sensor-based countermeasures, and (3) circuit-level design techniques. Fabrication-based countermeasures are costly and often incompatible with standard industrial manufacturing processes, limiting their practicality for OP-resilient chip design. Sensor-based countermeasures may be circumvented by adaptive attackers, whereas circuit-level techniques typically require modifications to the layout of standard-cell libraries. Such modifications are time-consuming and can introduce considerable PPA overheads relative to conventional standard-cell designs. Therefore, this study investigates whether increasing the local layout density around a target logic cell can enhance resilience against OP attacks without requiring modifications beyond the layout level. In this context, local density refers to the fraction of a predefined region surrounding the target cell that is occupied by neighboring logic cells and associated layout structures. Our methodology employs standard logic cells to protect the chip’s sensitive information from an adversary equipped with OP capabilities. We found that increasing the local density of surrounding logic cells near a target logic cell enhances overall reflection, effectively masking the reflection from the target logic cell. This can significantly improve the concealment of the secure cell’s information from the OP attack since the reflections from the neighboring logic cells overlap with the target logic cells that need to be secured. Hence, an adversary cannot distinguish the exact location of the source of reflection. We demonstrate that this methodology can effectively countermeasure against OP attacks by conducting detailed experiments on the relationship between density and reflection, using NAND, INVERTER, NOR, and Flip-Flop cells. We exhaustively evaluated thousands of placement strategies with varying densities to show the efficacy of our technique against OP attacks. Moreover, we demonstrate the integration of our OP attack mitigation technique into the ASIC flow for designing an AES-128 core. We demonstrate that our technique in the worst-case comes with a 1% increase in power consumption, a 1% increase in area, and no change in the operating frequency compared to the unprotected AES-128 core against OP attack.
doi:10.1145/3859873.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3859873.summary_zh: 针对光学探测攻击，提出通过选择性提高局部密度来隐藏芯片信息的电路级防护方法，避免修改标准单元库布局。摘要片段未披露具体实现细节与PPA开销的量化结果。
doi:10.1145/3859873.title: The Deception of Sight: Camouflaging Chips Information Against Optical Probing Attacks By Selective Increase of Local Density

doi:10.1145/3859878.abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have recently achieved major gains across many domains, increasing the need for hardware accelerators that can adapt to changing workloads. Because DNN layers have diverse characteristics, each may benefit from a different hardware architecture. FPGAs support this through runtime reconfiguration, but applying it to neural network accelerators remains limited. Reconfiguring the FPGA between every pair of layers would tailor hardware to each layer but incur prohibitive reconfiguration overhead. We address this by proposing a cluster-based approach that groups layers with similar computational requirements and assigns each group a shared hardware configuration. This reduces the number of reconfigurations while preserving efficient execution. However, selecting good clusters and configurations creates a large design space, especially for large networks: too few clusters merges dissimilar layers and hurts efficiency, while too many clusters increases reconfiguration overhead. To tackle this, we present a Design-Space Exploration (DSE) framework that co-optimizes clustering schemes and hardware configurations using genetic algorithms. Our method explores clustering schemes without accuracy loss, as the network and numeric precision remain fixed. Unlike prior work that optimizes only hardware or only mapping, our approach jointly optimizes both. We show that reconfiguring at carefully chosen points reduces overall inference latency despite reconfiguration costs. On GPT-2, ResNet-18, VGG01, VGG02, and AlexNet, our cluster-based designs reduce latency by 20–43% versus a fixed architecture and outperform the Simba and Eyeriss accelerators on four of five models while matching performance on VGG02.
doi:10.1145/3859878.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3859878.summary_zh: 针对运行时部分重构FPGA上的DNN加速器，提出基于聚类的层分组与硬件配置协同设计空间探索框架，用遗传算法减少重构开销。给定摘要片段未披露具体加速比或资源数据。
doi:10.1145/3859878.title: Design-Space Exploration for Runtime-Reconfigurable FPGA-Based DNN Accelerators

doi:10.1145/3859884.abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) expedites accelerator customization by delivering a high-level hardware programming paradigm and offering a rich set of optimization directives. However, the quality of HLS designs is highly dependent on the designers’ selection of directives in the trade-off between different design metrics, which is non-trivial and can lead to a large design turnaround time. Design space exploration (DSE) serves as a promising solution to this problem, but existing studies on DSE suffer from a lack of scalability for large-scale applications and often spend a substantial portion of the exploration budget on costly design points. To address this problem, this paper proposes AutoShrink 2.0 , a DSE engine that adaptively shrinks the large search space of an HLS design to gradually retain only high-quality solutions. AutoShrink 2.0 incorporates (1) a comprehensive design space pruning strategy that integrates the joint effect of directives and domain knowledge, (2) an importance-guided Pareto optimization algorithm which dynamically traces the importance ranking of the applied directives and leverages this ranking to navigate the search direction of Pareto frontiers, and (3) a cost-aware post-filtering mechanism to screen out candidates that are computationally expensive yet of limited gain, reducing runtime overhead within a single evaluation. Experimental results on Vitis HLS demonstrate that AutoShrink 2.0 achieves an average distance to reference set (ADRS) of 8.40% across multiple applications with design spaces containing up to \(\text{10}^\text{16} \) design points, outperforming three heuristic methods and three state-of-the-art approaches by 8.01 × and 6.24 ×, respectively. On timeout-prone benchmarks, the cost-aware post-filtering strategy reduces the average timeout ratio by 66.1% compared with the variant without this strategy. Furthermore, design tool transfer experiments from Vitis HLS to Catapult HLS demonstrate the promising cross-tool applicability of AutoShrink 2.0.
doi:10.1145/3859884.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
doi:10.1145/3859884.summary_zh: 提出 AutoShrink 2.0 HLS 设计空间探索引擎，结合指令联合效应与领域知识剪枝，并用重要性引导的 Pareto 优化动态调整搜索方向。目标是在大规模应用中减少昂贵设计点开销并提升可扩展性；给定摘要片段未披露具体 PPA 数值。
doi:10.1145/3859884.title: AutoShrink 2.0: Automating Large-Scale Pareto Optimization in HLS via Adaptive and Cost-Aware Search Space Shrinkage

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: The Boolean Satisfiability problem (SAT) is a fundamental problem in computer science. While standard SAT solvers focus on finding a single solution, domains such as semiformal verification and software testing require generating multiple, diverse solutions to enhance testing effectiveness. Particularly in semiformal verification, utilizing such diverse solutions has proven effective in uncovering latent errors in complex designs that evade simulation and formal verification. This requirement gives rise to the Diverse SAT problem, which aims to generate a set of k solutions with the sum of pairwise Hamming distances as large as possible. In this paper, we present SATDiv, an advanced solver designed to effectively address the Diverse SAT problem. We conducted extensive experiments on public benchmarks derived from real-world applications in both hardware semiformal verification and software testing. The experimental results demonstrate that SATDiv outperforms state-of-the-art Diverse SAT solvers.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 针对半形式验证与软件测试中需要多个多样化解的需求，提出求解Diverse SAT问题的SATDiv求解器，以最大化k个解两两汉明距离之和为目标。在来自硬件半形式验证与软件测试的真实基准上实验表明，SATDiv优于当前最先进的Diverse SAT求解器。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: SATDiv: An Effective Solver for Diverse SAT Problem

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Isabelle/HOL is a widely used proof assistant for higher-order logic. However, constructing an Isabelle/HOL proof is not always straightforward. In particular, the user may not know which intermediate lemmas or assumptions are required. A common situation is that a user attempts a proof, the automated reasoning tools fail to find one, and the system returns only “No proof found.” This can be frustrating. A more helpful outcome would provide insight into (1) what is missing or (2) which reasoning steps the automated tools attempted. The first aspect corresponds to abduction: finding additional premises that would make the goal provable. The second aspect can be supported by reporting the facts that were relevant during the (ultimately unsuccessful) proof search. In this work, we present IsaAbduct, a new command for Isabelle/HOL that integrates an abductive reasoning engine to suggest plausible missing assumptions and to provide additional feedback about the proof search process. The command is based on the syntax-guided synthesis (SyGuS) solver cvc5 and the saturation-based prover E, and operates by exchanging grammar-based hypotheses from cvc5’s enumeration and relevant facts extracted from E’s saturation search, so that cvc5 and E synergistically guide each other’s progress. Our evaluation shows that IsaAbduct produces a variety of useful hypotheses for the user and indicates that the different backend configurations are complementary: the integrated approach leads to higher-quality suggestions in comparison with using either the cvc5 or the E pipeline in isolation. Index Terms—abduction; proof assistants; Isabelle/HOL; SMT; saturation.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出 Isabelle/HOL 的溯因推理命令 IsaAbduct，基于 cvc5 与 E 求解器建议缺失假设。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: IsaAbduct: A Multi-Strategy Abduction Pipeline for Isabelle/HOL

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Detecting semantic literal equivalences in propositional satisfiability (SAT) instances is an essential ingredient for Combinational Equivalence Checking (CEC), i.e., determining whether two combinational circuits are equivalent. Recent works highlighted clausal SAT sweeping as a viable and efficient approach for detecting such semantic equivalences. We present a careful parallelization of SAT sweeping that scales to hundreds of cores and significantly accelerates the equivalence sweeping process. Furthermore, we demonstrate how this scalable sweeping can be integrated seamlessly in an existing massively parallel SAT solver as a means of scalable preprocessing for CEC inputs.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 针对组合等价性检查中的语义文字等价检测，提出可扩展至数百核的并行 SAT sweeping 方法，并集成到大规模并行 SAT 求解器作为预处理。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Parallel SAT Sweeping on CNFs

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Property Directed Reachability (PDR) is a commonly used technique for automated hardware model checking, yet efficiently parallelizing it remains a significant challenge. Existing approaches, such as lemma sharing, often suffer from limited scalability as processor counts increase. In this work, we present two novel sharing-based parallelization strategies, preemptive propagation and ARPOS, and compare their performance with classical lemma sharing. To this end, we develop an asynchronous MPI-based message passing framework for the state-of-the-art rIC3 hardware model checker. Experimental results on the 2025 Hardware Model Checking Competition benchmark demonstrate that our preemptive propagation strategy yields a significant performance boost over classical lemma sharing.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 面向硬件模型检查的 PDR 并行化，提出 preemptive propagation 与 ARPOS 两种共享策略，并在 rIC3 上实现基于 MPI 的异步消息传递框架。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Beyond Lemma Sharing – Novel Parallelization Strategies for PDR

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Runtime verification enables checking temporal logic specifications over individual execution traces and offers a scalable alternative to exhaustive formal verification. In practice, systems must satisfy dozens to hundreds of temporal properties simultaneously; however, existing approaches monitor each property in isolation, resulting in redundant computation and limited scalability. In this work, we present an online multi-property monitoring framework that compiles past-time LTL and MTL specifications into a shared directed acyclic graph of subformulas with one output per property. Unlike prior approaches that construct monitors independently, our method extends compositional sequential network-based temporal logic monitor construction to a shared setting, enabling reuse of intermediate results across properties while preserving their individual structure. Central to our approach is a data-oriented execution model based on an arena-allocated, double-buffered layout that stores intermediate results for each subformula in compact, contiguous memory. This design favors spatial locality and enables incremental updates with minimal overhead. Experimental results demonstrate per-property throughput improvements of 2× to 4.5× and 6× to 12× in multi-property configurations compared to conventional single-property monitoring, enabling scalability to large specification sets and deployment in high-performance and resource-constrained systems.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出在线多属性运行时验证框架，将 past-time LTL 与 MTL 规约编译为共享子公式 DAG，并采用 arena 分配双缓冲布局复用中间结果。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Multi-Property Temporal Logic Monitoring

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Constrained specification mining enables the automatic discovery of desired properties from system traces. Generalized Reactivity of Rank 1, or GR(1), is a fragment of LTL with polynomial-time synthesis that natively encodes assume-guarantee properties present in most hardware and robotics domains. In this paper, we present GR1MINE, a SAT-based tool for efficiently learning GR(1) formulas from examples. We exploit the GR(1) temporal skeleton to incrementally enumerate formula candidates, leveraging learnt clauses to avoid recomputation. On the Boolean GR(1) Syntech suite, GR1MINE learns a realizable formula for all 60 benchmarks over 30× faster than generic and constrained LTL mining tools. On non-GR(1) specifications from SYNTCOMP, GR1MINE is still able to recover >2× more realizable specifications than baselines within the timeout.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出 SAT 工具 GR1MINE，从执行轨迹中学习 GR(1) 时序规约，利用 GR(1) 时序骨架增量枚举候选并复用学习子句。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Learning GR(1) Specifications from Traces

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Maintaining consistency between natural language documentation of business rules and their evolving internal implementations is a significant challenge in large-scale systems. We present SIRNA, a tool and framework for checking such consistency using SMT solvers. Using the case study of cost calculations in tax domains, we demonstrate a three-part system that combines large language models (LLMs) with formal verification methods. SIRNA translates natural language documentation into candidate SMT formulas using LLMs, followed by checks to validate the translations. Then, corresponding business rules are converted into equivalent SMT representations and validated against the natural language formalizations. Our method is generalizable to domains where business logic exists in both natural language documentation and programmatic implementation. Compared to baseline evaluations, SIRNA significantly reduces the number of false positives and false negatives while offering explainability for its findings.

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出 SIRNA，用 LLM 与 SMT 求解器检查自然语言业务规则与程序实现的一致性。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Verifiable Checks for Business Rule Consistency

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: We study the computational complexity of deciding reachability in symbolic transition systems represented in quantifier-free first-order logic with bit-vectors and arrays. It is known that without arrays, the problem is PSPACE-complete (resp. EXPSPACE-complete) if the bit-widths are encoded in unary (resp. binary). We show that the problem becomes EXPSPACE-complete (resp. 2-EXPSPACE-complete in the binary case) when arrays indexed by bit-vectors are present, even if array values are limited to bit-vector sorts. Further, we show that the problem is NONELEMENTARY if we allow arrays indexed by other arrays.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: On the Complexity of Word-Level Model Checking with Arrays

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Property-Directed Reachability (PDR/IC3) is widely used for hardware safety verification. Most implementations optimize time-to-answer, but certified workflows also require compact, inexpensive-to-check, and reproducible certificates. We introduce CAPDR, whose ranker is fitted offline on a disjoint development corpus, frozen, and used only to order PDR-generated proposals on unseen instances to target solving time, certificate size, and checker time. The ranker remains outside the trusted computing base: it cannot bypass the SAT guards on blocker insertion and pushing; obligation scheduling remains fair, and every SAFE/UNSAFE claim requires independent checker acceptance. CAPDR also defines certificate-centric metrics and replay logs for artifact-grade reproducibility. On the 2024 Hardware Model Checking Competition bit-level safety benchmarks, CAPDR solves six more instances than the same PDR engine with ranking disabled. Across each configuration’s checker-accepted solved set, the medians of the certificate-size proxy and checker time decrease by 24.6% and 49%, respectively. After the same post-hoc minimizer is applied to paired SAFE outputs, CAPDR certificates still contain 16.3% fewer literals and have 38.5% lower checker time. Index Terms—Hardware model checking, property-directed reachability, proof-carrying verification, certificate checking, learning-guided heuristics
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出证书感知的 PDR 方法 CAPDR，用离线训练的排序器指导 PDR 提案排序，同时保持排序器在可信计算基之外并需独立检查器接受。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Certificate-Aware Property-Directed Reachability

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: The upcoming IEEE P3109 standard for low-precision floating-point arithmetic can become the foundation of future machine learning hardware and software. Unlike IEEE-754, P3109 introduces a parametric framework defined by bitwidth, precision, signedness, and domain. This flexibility yields a vast combinatorial space of formats, some with as little as one bit of precision, alongside novel features such as stochastic rounding and saturation arithmetic. These deviations create a unique verification gap that this paper intends to address. This paper presents FLoPS, Formalization in Lean of the P3109 Standard, which is a formal model of P3109 in Lean. Our work serves as a rigorous, machine-checked specification that facilitates deep analysis of the standard. We demonstrate the model’s utility by verifying foundational properties and analyzing key algorithms within the P3109 context. Specifically, we reveal that FastTwoSum exhibits a novel property of computing the exact “overflow error” under saturation using any rounding mode, whereas previously established properties of the ExtractScalar algorithm fail for formats with one bit of precision. We also provide a verified executable bit-level kernel, with refinement proofs for rounding, saturation, projection, and the core arithmetic operations. This work provides a verified foundation for reasoning about P3109 and enables formal verification of future numerical hardware and software. Our Lean development is open source and publicly available.

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 在 Lean 中形式化 IEEE P3109 低精度浮点标准，验证基础性质并分析 FastTwoSum 与 ExtractScalar 等算法。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Semantics, Operations, and Properties of P3109 Floating-Point Representations in Lean

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Tapped delay lines (TDLs) implemented in field-programmable gate array (FPGA) carry-chain primitives are central to high-resolution time-to-digital converters (TDCs). However, TDLs are prone to bubble errors, i.e., local thermometer-code violations caused by implementation-dependent delay inversions and metastability, which are still treated largely by empirical post-silicon filtering rather than by design-time proof. We present an ordering-relation abstraction for formal verification of bubble behaviour in an explicit abstract threshold model. The abstraction replaces continuous delay magnitudes with a finite Boolean domain over adjacent tap orderings, thereby enabling exhaustive symbolic analysis of ordering-dependent safety properties. The method is instantiated on a reference 8-tap CARRY8-based TDL and verified in three phases: binary decision diagram (BDD)-based model checking in NuSMV, cross-solver validation in nuXmv, and IC3/PDR-based scaling to larger TDL chains. The verification establishes five structural results in the model: local bubble-inversion causality, mutual exclusion of simultaneous raw bubbles, monotonicity of three-tap majority suppression, structural survival of boundary bubbles under suppression, and reachability of recovery from sampled-bubble states. These results provide assumption-qualified design-time checks and decoder/filtering guidance that complement simulation and post-silicon characterisation.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 针对 FPGA CARRY8 抽头延迟线中的气泡错误，提出序关系抽象将连续延迟量化为相邻抽头序关系的有限布尔域，并在 NuSMV/nuXmv 中用 BDD 模型检查与 IC3/PDR 验证 8 抽头参考设计。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Ordering-Relation Abstraction for Formal Verification of Bubble Errors in CARRY8-Based Tapped Delay Lines

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Verifying retiming followed by additional sequential resynthesis steps remains challenging for existing tools, limiting aggressive optimizations. Commonly-used equivalence checking tools rely on internal resynthesis operations and error-prone orchestration of different model checkers, which makes certification difficult or even infeasible. We present an IC3-based technique that uses retiming as a preprocessing step and uses simulation to generate suspected invariants. Our technique efficiently verifies sequential equivalence problems under retiming and arbitrarily strong sequential resynthesis, and has the additional feature of producing certificates all the same. Our results on a selection of retimed and resynthesized open circuit designs show that our rather simple approach vastly outperforms the whole portfolio of the winner of the latest Hardware Model Checking Competition as a representative of general-purpose certifying model checkers. Compared to non-certifying approaches, like the mature equivalence checker of ABC, we are still competitive with additional complementary strengths.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出基于IC3的顺序等价性验证技术，以重定时为预处理并用仿真生成候选不变式，可处理重定时及任意强度的顺序再综合，同时产出证书。在重定时并再综合的开放电路设计上，该方法大幅优于最新硬件模型检测竞赛冠军的通用可认证模型检测器组合，并与ABC成熟等价检查器相比仍具竞争力且能力互补。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Certified Sequential Sweep Without Unrolling

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: While bounded model checking (BMC) is now standard practice for digital designs, analog/mixed-signal (AMS) hardware remains largely outside the reach of automated formal analysis. This class of problems requires heavyweight theory solvers that support nonlinear real arithmetic and ordinary differential equations (ODEs) to analyze circuit behavior and contains much more complex SAT constraints than classic hybrid systems problems as a result of digital control logic. SMT solvers supporting this theory, such as dReal, face a structural bottleneck when targeting AMS BMC problems: repetitive constraints arise across digital clock cycles and reused instantiations of modular hardware blocks. This causes the solver to frequently rediscover nearly the same theory lemmas with only the names of constants changed. We present DRPM, a domain-specific optimization that intercepts theory-solver explanations and, via free constant renaming (α-equivalence), injects a larger set of valid theory lemmas without additional theory-solver calls. The optimization is formalized within the Abstract DPLL⟨T ⟩ framework and proven sound and complete. DRPM is implemented in dReal via an efficient one-to-many pattern matching algorithm using structural hashing and discrimination trees. We evaluate DRPM on 6,562 nonlinear AMS and hybrid systems BMC benchmarks. With pattern matching enabled, DRPM achieves a 2.1×–7.4× PAR-2 speedup, with no increase in memory footprint. DRPM is available via open-source repository, and provides a drop-in 7.5×–11.4× end-to-end speedup on BMC problems over dReal3, the current state-of-the-art QF_NRA_ODE solver.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 针对模拟混合信号硬件的SMT有界模型检测，提出DRPM优化：拦截理论求解器解释，通过自由常量重命名（α等价）注入更多有效理论引理而无需额外求解器调用，并在Abstract DPLL⟨T⟩框架下证明其可靠与完备，已在dReal中实现。给定摘要片段未披露具体基准与量化加速结果。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Lemma Pattern Matching for SMT-based Verification of Analog Mixed-Signal Hardware

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Formal verification of digital hardware designs is a well established practice in the semiconductor industry. However, designs combining digital and analog components (mixed-signal designs) remain with limited application of formal verification due to the complexity of automating proofs on the continuous state space of analog systems. In this work we perform a case study of formal verification for mixed-signal designs where we instrumentalize Yosys, an industrial-grade SystemVerilog compiler, and Pono, a state-of-the-art word-level model checker, to implement a formal verification flow on a set of 31 realistic mixed-signal benchmarks that we crafted from testbenches for analog blocks using real number modeling. As the practice of abstracting the analog domain with real-valued variables in SystemVerilog is already common place on simulation, we propose an interpretation of such verification problems on the theory of real arithmetic, which enables order of magnitude verification speed-ups using SMT solvers relative to the traditional bit-blasting interpretation on the theory of floating-point arithmetic. Despite the semantic differences between the two theories, our benchmarks indicate that mixed-signal hardware verification problems are not dependent on floating-point arithmetic details in practice, which favors the adoption of real arithmetic solvers. To demonstrate the practicality of this method, we perform a comparative analysis of the results from different theories over our benchmark set and discuss the technical trade-offs that arise when introducing formal verification to the mixed-signal verification domain.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Formal Verification of Mixed-Signal Systems Using Real Number Modeling with SMT-based Model Checking

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: The Move Prover (MVP) is a formal verifier for smart contracts written in the Move programming language. Recently, Move on Aptos was extended with higher-order functions: imperative functions as first-class values that can be passed around, stored in data structs, and kept in persistent storage, enabling dynamic dispatch. This paper describes the representation of function values in the Move specification language and their implementation in MVP. We introduce behavioral predicates which characterize Move functions (aborts and pre- /postconditions) by single-state or two-state predicates. We also introduce state labels for naming intermediate memory states in which expressions are evaluated and which allow to compose behavioral predicates to describe sequences of state transitions. On SMT level, function values are encoded by discriminating over the possible function values reaching a call site: when the concrete function is known, its effect is accounted for directly; when it is unknown (for example, a function parameter, or a closure loaded from storage), its behavioral predicates describe the effect. Our approach goes beyond, for example, Dafny, by supporting imperative first-class functions which can modify state via Rust-style references and global variables, and leads to more efficient SMT encodings than separation logic because of the static separation of memory enabled by Move. We further extend MVP’s specification inference tool to work with function values: given arbitrary higher-order Move code, weakest-precondition analysis semi-automatically derives behavioral-predicate-based specifications, reducing the annotation burden and providing a validation pipeline for the new specification constructs.

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Formal Verification of Imperative First-Class Functions in Move

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: How do LLMs compare with symbolic tools on program synthesis tasks? We investigate this question on several synthesis domains: LTL reactive synthesis, syntax-guided synthesis, distributed protocol synthesis, and recursive function synthesis. For each domain, we choose a state-of-the-art symbolic tool and compare it to an open-source, 32 billion parameter version of the QWEN LLM and the proprietary, frontier LLM GPT-5. We couple QWEN with a symbolic verifier and run it repeatedly until it either produces a solution that passes the verifier, or until there is a timeout, for each benchmark. We run GPT-5 once per benchmark and verify the generated output. In all domains, the symbolic tools solve more benchmarks than QWEN and either outperform or are about on par with GPT-5. In terms of execution time, the symbolic tools outperform QWEN and GPT-5 in all domains, despite the fact that the LLMs are run on significantly more powerful hardware.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 在LTL反应式综合、语法引导综合、分布式协议综合与递归函数综合等任务上比较LLM与符号工具，符号工具解题更多且执行时间更优。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: Can LLMs Perform Synthesis?

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Hybrid games model cyber-physical systems (CPS), like cars, trains, and airplanes, where discrete control decisions interact with continuous physical dynamics. We use Large Language Models (LLMs) to scale formal verification and synthesis for hybrid systems and games in a high-level symbolic logic, differential game logic (dGL). This combination of a logic with the right expressivity and automation of the interactive theorem proving process using LLMs brings within reach a challenging class of CPS verification/synthesis problems that were previously well out of range of automatic theorem proving. We demonstrate it on five challenging case studies, all beyond the reach of existing automatic techniques. Verification succeeds for all five, and the synthesis of control solutions succeeds for four of the five.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 用LLM辅助微分博弈逻辑中的交互式定理证明，对五个信息物理系统案例完成验证、四个完成控制综合。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: LLM-Powered Automatic Theorem Proving and Synthesis for Hybrid Systems and Games

doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.abstract: Assertion-based verification (ABV) uses SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) to formally specify design behavior, but constructing high-quality SVA properties remains a labor-intensive and error-prone process. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled automated SVA generation from design specification documents; however, there are limitations in how the quality of the generated SVA properties, and thus the SVA generator, is evaluated. Existing automatic evaluation methods rely on formal tools – such as model checking and coverage analysis – to measure the correctness and completeness of the generated properties against a golden RTL implementation. However, it is difficult to obtain bug-free RTL designs, and even if they are available, the computed metrics do not accurately reflect the quality of generated properties against design specifications. We propose SVAEVAL, an automatic approach to evaluate SVA property generators, by directly evaluating the generated property sets without the need of golden RTL implementations. SVAEVAL considers two different scenarios: (1) If a human-expert-generated golden SVA property set is available (e.g., in a benchmark set), a formal framework is used to accurately evaluate the quality of the generated property set against the golden set. (2) Without a golden SVA property set, a hybrid formal and LLM-based framework is used to compare the quality of two generated property sets from different SVA generators. Experimental results demonstrate that SVAEVAL provides significantly more reliable evaluation than prior approaches, and offer new insights into the capabilities and limitations of various LLM-based SVA property generators.
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.journal: Proceedings of the 26th Conference on Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2026)
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.summary_zh: 提出SVAEval，无需黄金RTL即可自动评估LLM生成的SystemVerilog断言属性集质量，覆盖有专家黄金SVA属性集与无黄金参考两种场景，并借助形式化方法进行评价。针对现有依赖模型检测与覆盖率、需无缺陷RTL且指标不能准确反映规范符合度的评估局限。给定摘要片段未披露具体评估结果。
doi:10.34727/2026/isbn.978-3-85448-093-8.title: SVAEval: An Evaluation Framework for LLM-based SVA Property Generators
